EVENTS.h: Drive-by gunman kills one, wounds four west of Paris; terror inquiry opened
EVENTS.s: A man opened fire from a vehicle at multiple people along his route in Trappes and neighbouring La Verrière, about 20 km west of Paris, at around 10:30 on 23 October, killing one person and wounding four, before being arrested in nearby Coignières. The interior minister said the shootings occurred at three separate locations with what appeared to be a military-grade or automatic weapon, and the Trappes mayor said the gunman fired at passers-by, including at a playground. France's National Anti-Terrorism Prosecutor opened an investigation into murder in connection with a terrorist enterprise aggravated by the victim's actual or perceived race, ethnicity, nationality or religion.
EVENTS.impl: Workable with advance · curfew-aware movement planning, avoid protest perimeters. France's risk rose on the eve of the 24 October protest day: a gunman firing an automatic weapon from a car killed one person and seriously wounded four, including a 12-year-old, at three locations in Trappes and La Verrière west of Paris on the morning of 23 October before his arrest in Coignières, and the national anti-terrorism prosecutor opened a murder-in-connection-with-terrorism inquiry with a racial aggravating circumstance, which Macron called a racist terrorist attack.

EVENTS.h: Daytime drone raid on Moscow shuts all four airports, Sheremetyevo sheltered
EVENTS.s: Moscow Mayor Sergei Sobyanin said air defences had destroyed nine drones flying towards Moscow by 13:39 on 23 October, with emergency crews working at debris sites, after 155 drones were sent towards the Moscow region overnight and five downed on approach to the capital. Rosaviatsia halted arrivals and departures at Sheremetyevo, Domodedovo, Vnukovo and Zhukovsky in the afternoon, Sheremetyevo declared an air-raid alert and moved passengers into shelters, and Sobyanin later put the afternoon tally at 21 drones downed over two hours.
EVENTS.impl: No-go · active deep-strike campaign and arbitrary detention. Russia's two principal cities remain under sustained Ukrainian drone attack: after the 18 October assault that killed one and injured 15 in St Petersburg and set the oil terminal ablaze, 630 drones were sent towards Moscow overnight on 21-22 October wounding two, and on 23 October a daytime raid forced Rosaviatsia to halt flights at all four Moscow airports and Sheremetyevo to move passengers into shelters, with Mayor Sobyanin reporting 155 drones towards the region overnight and more than 20 downed on approach to the city during the afternoon.

EVENTS.h: Oromia-Somali fighting in Moyale kills at least nine; 2,500 flee into Kenya
EVENTS.s: Fighting between Oromo and Somali forces in the Ethiopian border town of Moyale began on 21 October and gunfire could still be heard on 23 October, residents told Reuters. An official at Moyale hospital on the Ethiopian side said about 30 wounded, mostly by heavy weapons, had been brought in and that four died on 22 October and five on 23 October. Marsabit county commissioner Stanley Kamande said at least 2,500 displaced Ethiopians were staying in the Kenyan town of Moyale, where a stray bullet lodged in a local woman's neck.
EVENTS.impl: No-go north of Addis · Addis essential travel with advance. Tigray is easing but not settled: federal forces and the allied Tigray Peace Force hold Mekelle, Adigrat, Adwa and Axum, shops and banks were reopening in Mekelle on 22 October and schools are due to resume on 26 October under the six-month caretaker administration Abiy named on 16 October, yet the TPLF rejects it, Abiy warned Eritrea on 19 October of 'very severe consequences' if it keeps backing his enemies, and troops face each other along the Eritrean border.

EVENTS.h: 18-storey building under construction collapses in Nairobi's Eastleigh; seven missing
EVENTS.s: A multi-storey building under construction collapsed at about 13:40 on 23 October on 9th Street in Eastleigh, a dense commercial and residential district of Nairobi, with shops operating on its occupied ground floor. Interior minister Kipchumba Murkomen said late on 23 October that 66 of the 67 workers on site escaped unharmed, one was injured and seven people had been reported missing; police rescued one woman from the rubble and fired tear gas to disperse looters targeting nearby shops. Search and rescue by the Kenya Red Cross, the National Disaster Management Unit and the KDF disaster response battalion continued into the night.
EVENTS.impl: Workable with advance · health screening. Nairobi and the main business corridors are operating, but 23 October brought two shocks to the capital: an 18-storey building under construction collapsed onto occupied ground-floor shops in Eastleigh at about 13:40, with seven people reported missing, two injured and police firing tear gas at looters, and the health ministry announced a second Ebola death, a 65-year-old relative of the index patient who fell ill in quarantine, in a nine-case cluster that still shows no transmission outside the family and healthcare-worker group.

EVENTS.h: UN: Ebola at 9,765 cases, 4,727 deaths in eight provinces; Nigeria case confirmed
EVENTS.s: UN agencies said on 23 October that the Bundibugyo Ebola outbreak in DRC had reached 9,765 confirmed cases and 4,727 deaths across eight provinces, the latest being Nord-Ubangi, with 30,000 contacts under daily monitoring. WHO's incident manager warned the virus 'will resurge very quickly' if the response slackens and said patients in insecure parts of eastern DRC visit two to five facilities before referral. Nigeria confirmed its first imported case on 20 October and Kenya has reported nine cases including one death.
EVENTS.impl: No-go · east (Kivus, Ituri) active conflict; Kinshasa workable with advance. Rating held at 4.

EVENTS.adm: Nationwide (Paris, Lyon, Marseille, Nice, Montpellier, Orléans)
EVENTS.h: 70,000 police for 24 October protests; bans in Lyon, Nice, Montpellier
EVENTS.s: Interior Minister Laurent Nuñez said on 23 October that some 70,000 security personnel, about 20% more than a week earlier, would be deployed across France for Saturday's protests, warning that calls for violence and looting were circulating on social media. All demonstrations were banned in Lyon, Nice and Montpellier, Paris marches were limited to a Bastille-Nation route, a union march in Marseille was allowed on an exceptional basis, a 20,000-30,000-strong counter-protest to the National Rally congress in Orléans was barred from the city centre, and the Louvre and other major Paris museums closed. High-school student groups meeting Macron for the first time urged pupils to keep mobilising; courts have jailed 217 people over the 17 October violence.
EVENTS.impl: Workable with advance · curfew-aware movement planning, avoid protest perimeters. France's risk rose on the eve of the 24 October protest day: a gunman firing an automatic weapon from a car killed one person and seriously wounded four, including a 12-year-old, at three locations in Trappes and La Verrière west of Paris on the morning of 23 October before his arrest in Coignières, and the national anti-terrorism prosecutor opened a murder-in-connection-with-terrorism inquiry with a racial aggravating circumstance, which Macron called a racist terrorist attack.

EVENTS.h: UN rights chief: drone strikes killed at least 306 in Sudan in three weeks
EVENTS.s: UN Human Rights Chief Volker Türk said on 23 October that his office had documented at least 306 deaths and hundreds of injuries from drone strikes attributed to both the army and the RSF in the first three weeks of October, hitting homes, markets, hospitals, displacement sites, power stations and water sources in Kordofan, Darfur, Blue Nile and Khartoum. It put the 18 October double-tap strike on a transport truck at Dibab, West Kordofan, at 139 dead, and flagged RSF retaliatory strikes on Khartoum including the airport area as an emerging trend.
EVENTS.impl: No-go · active conflict. Sudan's war is in a drone-dominated phase: the UN Human Rights Office said on 23 October it had documented at least 306 deaths from drone strikes by both sides in the first three weeks of October alone, including a double-tap strike on a transport hub at Dibab in West Kordofan on 18 October that it now puts at 139 dead, army strikes on Nyala and RSF retaliation on Khartoum including the airport district on 19 October, and the 19 October strike on Abyei's Amiet market across the South Sudan border, which Khartoum denied on 22 October.

EVENTS.h: UN Security Council condemns Abyei drone strikes as UNISFA verifies at least 80 dead
EVENTS.s: The UN Security Council on 23 October condemned in the strongest terms the 19 October drone attacks near Amiet Market and Todach, said the toll was expected to rise as UNISFA continued to verify casualties, called for a full, transparent and prompt investigation and reaffirmed that Abyei must remain demilitarised and free of all forces except UNISFA. UNISFA's updated statement of 22 October put the verified toll at at least 80 killed with 27 injured treated by UN personnel, and said it was engaging Khartoum and Juba ahead of a Joint Political and Security Mechanism meeting scheduled in Khartoum.
EVENTS.impl: No-go outside Juba · essential travel only. South Sudan is absorbing direct spillover from Sudan's drone war: the 19 October strike on Amiet market and Todach in Abyei killed at least 80 by UNISFA's verified count on 22 October and 153 by the Abyei administration's figure given to Reuters, with many still missing; the UN Security Council condemned the attack in the strongest terms on 23 October, demanded an investigation and reaffirmed Abyei's demilitarised status, while Khartoum denied on 22 October that its armed forces were involved after Juba summoned Sudan's ambassador.

EVENTS.h: Kenya records second Ebola death as nine-case cluster stays within quarantine
EVENTS.s: Kenya's health ministry said late on 23 October that a 65-year-old woman, a close relative of the Kenyan man who died of Bundibugyo Ebola on 5 October, had died after developing symptoms while in quarantine, the country's second death. Kenya has confirmed nine cases, all linked to the index patient who travelled from DRC via Uganda, with all 135 listed contacts under follow-up as of 22 October; health officials are also investigating whether the first Kenyan and Nigerian patients crossed paths at Entebbe airport on 3 October.
EVENTS.impl: Workable with advance · health screening. Nairobi and the main business corridors are operating, but 23 October brought two shocks to the capital: an 18-storey building under construction collapsed onto occupied ground-floor shops in Eastleigh at about 13:40, with seven people reported missing, two injured and police firing tear gas at looters, and the health ministry announced a second Ebola death, a 65-year-old relative of the index patient who fell ill in quarantine, in a nine-case cluster that still shows no transmission outside the family and healthcare-worker group.

EVENTS.h: Lula and Bolsonaro clash in final debate as polls show 50-50 tie
EVENTS.s: President Lula and Senator Flávio Bolsonaro held their second and final televised debate on TV Globo in Rio de Janeiro on Friday night, two days before the 25 October runoff. A Datafolha survey published on Thursday showed the pair tied at 50% of voting intentions each, erasing Bolsonaro's four-point lead of two weeks earlier, and a Quaest poll after the first debate showed undecided voters had doubled from 7% to 14%. Both campaigns have petitions pending at the Superior Electoral Court seeking to disqualify the other.
EVENTS.impl: Workable with advance · Rio metro elevated through 25-26 Oct (federal troops in 15 municipalities); avoid favela-adjacent routes and Avenida Brasil at night; expect result-related gatherings in Brasília, São Paulo and Rio on Sunday night and possible court challenges to a narrow result. Brazil votes on Sunday 25 October in a presidential runoff that is a statistical dead heat: Datafolha published a 50-50 tie on 22 October and the final TV Globo debate on 23 October left the share of undecided voters doubling to 14% (AFP, 23 Oct), while each camp has a petition pending at the Superior Electoral Court to disqualify the other, so a narrow result is likely to be contested in court and on the street.

EVENTS.h: Federal troops join 20,000 police to secure Rio runoff vote in 15 municipalities
EVENTS.s: Army, navy and air force personnel will reinforce security in 15 Rio de Janeiro municipalities on Sunday 25 October at the request of the regional electoral court, approved by the Superior Electoral Court. They join more than 20,000 state security agents escorting voting machines, guarding polling stations and patrolling roads across the state, Brazil's third-largest electorate with over 12.8 million registered voters. The same arrangement was used in the first round on 4 October.
EVENTS.impl: Workable with advance · Rio metro elevated through 25-26 Oct (federal troops in 15 municipalities); avoid favela-adjacent routes and Avenida Brasil at night; expect result-related gatherings in Brasília, São Paulo and Rio on Sunday night and possible court challenges to a narrow result. EVENTS.h: Coalition fast-tracks public-media funding overhaul criticised as power grab
EVENTS.s: The Czech ruling coalition moved on 23 October to fast-track legislation that would shift financing of Czech Television and Czech Radio into the state budget and cut their funding by about 15%, possibly during next year, scrapping the 205-crown monthly licence fee. The bill was unexpectedly brought to a first reading and the lower house voted to extend debate into Saturday to overcome opposition obstruction. Critics say the plan threatens press independence; the government says savings are needed and editorial coverage will not be affected.
EVENTS.impl: Monitored · routine. No terrorism, sabotage, violent unrest or major transport disruption was confirmed in Czechia between 10 and 24 October.

EVENTS.h: Austria expels four Russian diplomats over suspected espionage; Moscow vows response
EVENTS.s: Austria's foreign ministry said on 23 October it was expelling four Vienna-based Russian diplomats over activities incompatible with their diplomatic status, a term usually used for spying, based on findings by the Austrian security authorities. Three worked at Russia's embassy to Austria and one at the Russian delegation to the OSCE; all were declared personae non gratae and ordered to leave. Russian news agencies cited a foreign ministry official saying Russia will respond, and the Russian embassy called the move a further unfriendly step.
EVENTS.impl: Monitored · routine. Austria's window closed with a counter-intelligence move rather than a security incident: on 23 October the foreign ministry declared four Vienna-based Russian diplomats, three at the embassy and one at the OSCE delegation, personae non gratae for activities incompatible with their status, and Moscow said it would respond.

EVENTS.h: Algeria orders halt to urea exports to France as diplomatic rift deepens
EVENTS.s: Algeria has instructed urea producers to stop exporting the fertiliser to France in an intensification of trade curbs that followed the diplomatic rift with its former colonial ruler, five diplomatic and industry sources told Reuters on 23 October. The French fertiliser association Afcome and wheat growers' group AGPB said the move could put at risk around 30% of France's urea imports, and six French and European diplomats said Algiers had imposed an unofficial near-blanket ban on French imports in late July. Several diplomats said Algeria denied the curbs when asked; the Algerian embassy in Paris did not respond to Reuters.
EVENTS.impl: Workable with advance · southern and eastern border zones restricted. No terrorist attack, clash or significant protest was wire-confirmed in Algeria between 10 and 24 October; the environment is stable but heavily securitised and the state continues to frame domestic problems as foreign-backed subversion.

EVENTS.h: Southern truckers ease roadblocks as cabinet approves diesel aid for hauliers
EVENTS.s: Truck drivers' protests that seriously affected fuel and food supplies in southern Italy were easing on 22 October, with hauliers saying roadblocks would be lifted in Sicily after talks with the government and drivers in Calabria suspending their protest, while a Campania spokesman hoped blockades around Naples would lift later that day. The cabinet approved a decree adding 106 million euros in tax credits for truck drivers hit by higher fuel costs and took a harder line against roadblocks, with police escorts for essential goods. Supermarkets, petrol stations and hospitals in Campania had suffered severe disruption.
EVENTS.impl: Workable with advance · avoid city-centre protest zones. Italy enters Saturday 24 October with security forces deploying massively for cost-of-living protests planned in eight cities including Rome and Milan, where 500 soldiers patrol under the 20 October decree that also created a violent-protest offence after the 17-18 October riots in Milan, Turin, Bologna, Brescia and Bergamo.

EVENTS.h: 630 drones sent towards Moscow overnight, two wounded; Lipetsk apartment blocks hit
EVENTS.s: Moscow Mayor Sobyanin said 630 Ukrainian drones were sent towards the capital overnight on 21-22 October, most downed at long range, and two people were wounded near Moscow; the Defence Ministry said 808 drones were downed across Russia. In Lipetsk, some 400 km south of Moscow, a man was injured as drones hit apartment buildings and a medical facility, Governor Artamonov said. The attacks came hours after Witkoff's talks with Putin in St Petersburg.
EVENTS.impl: No-go · active deep-strike campaign and arbitrary detention. Russia's two principal cities remain under sustained Ukrainian drone attack: after the 18 October assault that killed one and injured 15 in St Petersburg and set the oil terminal ablaze, 630 drones were sent towards Moscow overnight on 21-22 October wounding two, and on 23 October a daytime raid forced Rosaviatsia to halt flights at all four Moscow airports and Sheremetyevo to move passengers into shelters, with Mayor Sobyanin reporting 155 drones towards the region overnight and more than 20 downed on approach to the city during the afternoon.

EVENTS.h: Air strike on ELN camp in Cauca kills nine, including regional commander
EVENTS.s: Nine members of the ELN were killed on Thursday in a military bombing of a camp in rural El Tambo, Cauca, President Abelardo de la Espriella said on social media. He said the dead included alias Marcos Pacífico, one of the group's main leaders in south-west Colombia. It is the fifth air strike ordered since he took office on 7 August.
EVENTS.impl: Workable with advance · Bogotá/Medellín/Cartagena; no-go rural Cauca, Nariño, Catatumbo, Arauca and southern Cesar; avoid Pan-American Highway south of Cali and overland travel on the Venezuelan border. President de la Espriella's offensive against the ELN and FARC dissidents is escalating on both sides: a 22 October air strike on an ELN camp in El Tambo, Cauca killed nine guerrillas including regional commander alias Marcos Pacífico (DW, 23 Oct), the fifth bombing of his term, while guerrillas hit back at fixed police positions, wounding six officers in a drone-bomb attack on the Pelaya station in Cesar on 21 October (AP, 21 Oct) after the 12 October car bomb at the El Bordo toll plaza on the Pan-American Highway (AP, 12 Oct).

EVENTS.h: Ukrainian national arrested in Brandenburg on suspicion of spying for Russia
EVENTS.s: Federal prosecutors said a Ukrainian national identified as Vadym Y. was arrested in Brandenburg on 22 October on suspicion of spying for a Russian intelligence service via an intermediary since at least July 2025. He is accused of gathering information on the production of armoured vehicles, ammunition and explosives and on personnel and installations securing NATO's eastern flank, partly by approaching people in the European defence industry. Chancellor Merz said the arrest did not surprise him and warned there would be more such cases.
EVENTS.impl: Monitored · critical-infrastructure watch. Germany's state-threat environment hardened in the final week of the window: federal prosecutors arrested a Ukrainian national in Brandenburg on 22 October for gathering military intelligence for Russia, including on NATO eastern-flank sites and defence-industry production, one day after the Bundeswehr rated the Russian sabotage threat to its own forces as significant for the first time, and Chancellor Merz said on 22 October that Germany is the target of intensive espionage and more such cases will follow.

EVENTS.h: Police fire tear gas at Tunis suburb protesters after custody death; Sfax clashes
EVENTS.s: Tunisian police fired tear gas on Thursday 22 October to disperse protesters in Ettadhamen after the death of a man detained on suspicion of drug dealing, whose family said he died from police violence after arrest; local media cited a police source saying he swallowed drugs during a raid. Protesters blocked roads, burned tyres and threw stones at police, who moved to secure a National Guard station, and AFP reported the road blockades continued overnight into 23 October. Earlier the same day police clashed with protesters in Jebeniana after the death of a man his relatives say died during a security chase, with similar clashes in Agareb and a student protest in Sfax; the interior ministry did not comment.
EVENTS.impl: Workable · avoid central Tunis, Ettadhamen and Sfax-area flashpoints on protest days. Tunisia's risk profile is rising: on 22 October police fired tear gas at protesters in Ettadhamen, a suburb of Tunis, after the death of a man in custody, with parallel clashes in Jebeniana and Agareb in Sfax governorate and student protests in Sfax city (Reuters), and AFP reported on 23 October that protesters in Ettadhamen burned tyres and blocked roads overnight with no confirmed casualties or arrests, five days after the UGTT-led march of 17 October, the largest show of opposition to President Saied in years.

EVENTS.h: Egypt urges Yemen talks as parliament weighs defensive military support for Saudi Arabia
EVENTS.s: Foreign Minister Badr Abdelatty said on 22 October that Egypt wants to 'explore every opportunity' for a political solution to the Yemen conflict, ahead of the 26 October parliamentary vote on authorising the armed forces to support Saudi Arabia against the Houthis. Abdelatty and intelligence chief Hassan Rashad travelled to Riyadh on Wednesday 21 October to deliver a letter from President Sisi to Crown Prince Mohammed bin Salman; Sisi said the same day that any support would be limited to defending Saudi territory and borders and would not include an attack on Yemen. The Houthi-run parliament's speaker warned on 17 October that Egyptian involvement would pose 'a grave threat to its own national security and internal stability'.
EVENTS.impl: Workable · Red Sea/Suez watch; North Sinai and Sudan border restricted. No terrorist attack, Sinai incident or domestic unrest was wire-confirmed in Egypt between 10 and 24 October, but the external-security profile is rising.

EVENTS.h: Pipeline valve shut at Zawiya station cuts output at Hamada and Tahara oilfields
EVENTS.s: The head of the National Oil Corporation told Reuters on Thursday 22 October that a valve on the AGOCO pipeline carrying crude from the Hamada and Tahara oilfields to Zawiya port had been shut, reducing production at both fields. NOC said individuals entered the crude receiving station near the Zawiya refinery and closed the valve without coordination, warning that a continued shutdown 'will lead to the loss of volumes of crude oil production', and urged the authorities to intervene immediately to reopen the valve and secure the site. Hamada produces about 50,000 bpd under stable conditions; an armed group shut valve 7 on the Sharara-Zawiya pipeline for five days in September at a cost NOC put at $95 million.
EVENTS.impl: No-go for routine travel · essential only with armed escort and air evacuation plan. Libya remains Critical and the trend is rising: on 22 October individuals entered the AGOCO crude receiving station near the Zawiya refinery and shut the valve on the Hamada-Zawiya pipeline, cutting output at the Hamada and Tahara fields (Reuters) in the second forced pipeline closure in western Libya in five weeks, with no wire-confirmed reopening as of 24 October; on 21 October armed men stormed the National Audit Bureau in Tripoli to impose a disputed deputy head, drawing UNSMIL's strongest condemnation and a warning of targeted sanctions; and on 18 October an 82mm mortar blast killed at least nine Anti-Threat Security Agency personnel during training in Zawiya (Reuters).

EVENTS.adm: Caracas, Valencia, Maracay, San Cristóbal, Maracaibo
EVENTS.h: Thousands join first nationwide opposition protest in nearly two years
EVENTS.s: Thousands of Venezuelans marched on Thursday in Caracas and other cities in the first nationwide opposition protest since early 2025, demanding free elections by July 2027 and the release of political prisoners. The ruling Socialist Party called a march from Plaza Venezuela, the opposition's planned gathering point, two hours earlier, and Interior Minister Diosdado Cabello attended it while opposition supporters moved to a nearby location. Security forces kept a notably thin presence.
EVENTS.impl: Monitored · Caracas workable with advance; stand off from all demonstrations and party marches in central Caracas (Plaza Venezuela, Miraflores approaches), low profile, no overland border travel. The first nationwide opposition protest in nearly two years on 22 October passed without wire-reported violence, with thousands marching in Caracas, Valencia, Maracay, San Cristóbal and Maracaibo for a 2027 election date and the release of political prisoners while the ruling party staged a rival march from the same square (Reuters, 22 Oct); Machado's party afterwards said seven marchers were detained by the Bolivarian National Police (AFP, 23 Oct).

EVENTS.h: Shops and banks reopen in Mekelle as border communities fear wider war
EVENTS.s: Al Jazeera reported on 22 October that shops were reopening and banks resuming services in Mekelle under federal control, though residents remained anxious. Near the Eritrean border, military movements and conflicting accounts of troop deployments have heightened fears that the fighting could spread beyond Tigray; Ethiopia's foreign minister accused Eritrea on 8 October of sending troops up to 60 km into Tigray.
EVENTS.impl: No-go north of Addis · Addis essential travel with advance. Tigray is easing but not settled: federal forces and the allied Tigray Peace Force hold Mekelle, Adigrat, Adwa and Axum, shops and banks were reopening in Mekelle on 22 October and schools are due to resume on 26 October under the six-month caretaker administration Abiy named on 16 October, yet the TPLF rejects it, Abiy warned Eritrea on 19 October of 'very severe consequences' if it keeps backing his enemies, and troops face each other along the Eritrean border.

EVENTS.h: China and Djibouti call for Red Sea freedom of navigation as Yemen fighting escalates
EVENTS.s: China and Djibouti said in a joint statement after their foreign ministers met in Beijing that all countries should enjoy freedom of navigation in the Red Sea and through the Bab el-Mandeb Strait, expressing concern about the deteriorating security situation. The statement said major powers outside the region should respect the sovereignty of littoral states and avoid resorting to force. Djibouti sits opposite Yemen, where Iran-backed Houthis are battling Saudi-backed government forces for control of the whole Yemeni Red Sea coast.
EVENTS.impl: Monitored · transit hub. No violent security incident was recorded inside Djibouti between 10 and 24 October; the humanitarian load is the story, with UNHCR counting 3,836 refugees arrived from Yemen in Obock region by 17 October, an acute watery diarrhoea outbreak in the Markazi camp and the aftermath of the 8-9 October migrant shipwreck off Obock (139 dead, 84 missing per IOM), which now falls outside the two-week window.

EVENTS.h: Rodríguez receives opposition negotiator Figuera; Machado's party reports seven marchers detained
EVENTS.s: Acting President Delcy Rodríguez received Dinorah Figuera, head of the opposition delegation in the US-backed talks, at the presidential palace on Thursday, their first meeting, with National Assembly president Jorge Rodríguez also present. The delegations had closed the third round of talks on Wednesday by agreeing to review laws that keep dozens of opposition figures, including Nobel laureate María Corina Machado, barred from elected office, while setting no election date. After Thursday's march, Machado's party Vente Venezuela said seven workers who took part were detained by the Bolivarian National Police.
EVENTS.impl: Monitored · Caracas workable with advance; stand off from all demonstrations and party marches in central Caracas (Plaza Venezuela, Miraflores approaches), low profile, no overland border travel. EVENTS.h: Bundeswehr rates Russian sabotage threat 'significant' after explosive drone near air base
EVENTS.s: Germany's armed forces classified the threat of Russian sabotage against their troops and facilities as significant for the first time, the second-highest level on their internal scale, a defence ministry spokesperson confirmed on 21 October. The assessment was triggered by a crashed drone carrying high explosives found near Wunstorf air base in mid-September and cites drone overflights of the Arrow 3 site and a hidden camera at Minden rail station. Intelligence services expect further actions in the near future.
EVENTS.impl: Monitored · critical-infrastructure watch. Germany's state-threat environment hardened in the final week of the window: federal prosecutors arrested a Ukrainian national in Brandenburg on 22 October for gathering military intelligence for Russia, including on NATO eastern-flank sites and defence-industry production, one day after the Bundeswehr rated the Russian sabotage threat to its own forces as significant for the first time, and Chancellor Merz said on 22 October that Germany is the target of intensive espionage and more such cases will follow.

EVENTS.h: Special Operations Group raid near Somali border kills 11 al-Shabaab fighters
EVENTS.s: Kenya's Special Operations Group, supported by aerial assets, raided a makeshift al-Shabaab camp in the Esagur Cutline area near the Kenya-Somalia border, killing 11 militants and seriously wounding seven, the government's Kenya News Agency reported on 21 October. Intelligence indicated about 30 fighters had assembled there and were in the final stages of preparing an assault on a border village in Mandera county; the rest escaped into Somalia. Officers recovered three machine guns, more than 400 rounds of ammunition and documents including religious tax receipts.

EVENTS.impl: Workable with advance · health screening. Nairobi and the main business corridors are operating, but 23 October brought two shocks to the capital: an 18-storey building under construction collapsed onto occupied ground-floor shops in Eastleigh at about 13:40, with seven people reported missing, two injured and police firing tear gas at looters, and the health ministry announced a second Ebola death, a 65-year-old relative of the index patient who fell ill in quarantine, in a nine-case cluster that still shows no transmission outside the family and healthcare-worker group.

EVENTS.h: Finland takes government public web services offline over critical PHP flaws
EVENTS.s: Finland's state IT centre Valtori shut down the government's public web services on 21 October as a precautionary measure after two critical vulnerabilities were disclosed in the PHP programming language. Valtori said it had found no attempt to exploit the flaws and that the outage was not the result of a data breach; the National Land Survey and other agencies' sites were affected while patches were applied.
EVENTS.impl: Workable · avoid SE border zone during Russia strike nights. Finland is safe for travel and operations, but the south-eastern coast between Loviisa and the Russian border is subject to short-notice air and sea closures whenever Ukraine mounts large strikes on St Petersburg; the Defence Forces imposed such restrictions on three consecutive mornings on 16, 17 and 18 October with no drones crossing into Finland, and no new restrictions were reported on 22-24 October.

EVENTS.h: Missile fired at Iranian Kurdish opposition camp north-east of Erbil
EVENTS.s: A missile was fired at an Iranian Kurdish opposition camp north-east of Erbil on 21 October, security sources told Reuters. No casualties were reported. It followed Iranian drone strikes on exile camps in Erbil province on 8, 12 and 17 October.
EVENTS.impl: Restricted · essential travel with advance, Erbil under drone threat. The Kurdistan Region remains the most active theatre: a missile was fired at an Iranian Kurdish opposition camp north-east of Erbil on 21 October (Reuters), the latest in a series of Iranian strikes on exile camps on 8, 12 and 17 October, and Tehran's ambassador said on 20 October that Baghdad had agreed to expel or hand over the opposition groups (AFP), a claim absent from the Iraqi statement and rejected by the groups themselves.

EVENTS.h: Military court sentences opposition leader Olfa Hamdi to four years in prison
EVENTS.s: A military court sentenced Third Republic Party leader Olfa Hamdi, who holds US citizenship, to four years in prison on charges of plotting against state security and inciting the military to disobey orders, her lawyer Akram Moussa told Reuters on Wednesday 21 October. The sentence comprises two separate two-year terms and fines totalling 80,000 dinars ($26,000); Hamdi, a former Tunisair CEO detained at Tunis airport in February, was already sentenced to two years in March in a separate case. The charges stemmed from social media posts, her lawyer told AFP.
EVENTS.impl: Workable · avoid central Tunis, Ettadhamen and Sfax-area flashpoints on protest days. Tunisia's risk profile is rising: on 22 October police fired tear gas at protesters in Ettadhamen, a suburb of Tunis, after the death of a man in custody, with parallel clashes in Jebeniana and Agareb in Sfax governorate and student protests in Sfax city (Reuters), and AFP reported on 23 October that protesters in Ettadhamen burned tyres and blocked roads overnight with no confirmed casualties or arrests, five days after the UGTT-led march of 17 October, the largest show of opposition to President Saied in years.

EVENTS.h: Armed men storm National Audit Bureau in Tripoli to impose disputed deputy head
EVENTS.s: UNSMIL condemned 'in the strongest possible terms' the use of force and intimidation at the headquarters of the National Audit Bureau in Tripoli on 21 October in an attempt to install a disputed deputy head of the institution. The mission called for an immediate end to armed interference and the withdrawal of armed personnel from the premises, and warned that those responsible for attacks on state institutions 'risk being subjected to targeted sanctions' under Security Council resolutions. The Audit Bureau said it suspended work after the armed raid.
EVENTS.impl: No-go for routine travel · essential only with armed escort and air evacuation plan. Libya remains Critical and the trend is rising: on 22 October individuals entered the AGOCO crude receiving station near the Zawiya refinery and shut the valve on the Hamada-Zawiya pipeline, cutting output at the Hamada and Tahara fields (Reuters) in the second forced pipeline closure in western Libya in five weeks, with no wire-confirmed reopening as of 24 October; on 21 October armed men stormed the National Audit Bureau in Tripoli to impose a disputed deputy head, drawing UNSMIL's strongest condemnation and a warning of targeted sanctions; and on 18 October an 82mm mortar blast killed at least nine Anti-Threat Security Agency personnel during training in Zawiya (Reuters).

EVENTS.h: Austrian and Swiss women freed after 18 months' captivity in Niger reach Benghazi
EVENTS.s: Austrian aid worker Eva Gretzmacher, 76, and Swiss community worker Claudia Abbt, 69, kidnapped separately in Agadez in January and April 2025, were freed and arrived in Benghazi, Libya, on 21 October in an operation reportedly overseen by the Haftar family. Both governments confirmed the releases on 22 October; no group has claimed the abductions, though reports have linked them to Islamic State militants. The circumstances of the release were not disclosed.
EVENTS.impl: No-go · essential travel only with state-level clearance. The deadliest incident between 10 and 24 October hit the north rather than the jihadist-hit west: gunmen in three vehicles ambushed two escorted passenger buses on the Arlit-Agadez road on 20 October, killing at least 11 (AFP; the Agadez governor later put the toll at 12 including a soldier), on the only corridor used by mining and humanitarian traffic to the uranium belt, and the military escort aboard did not prevent it.

EVENTS.h: IOM warns 874,000 could be displaced by El Niño floods by December
EVENTS.s: IOM said on 21 October that projections with the Danish Refugee Council estimate 874,319 people could be displaced in Somalia between October and December, 92 per cent of them by flooding, as the Deyr rains arrive under strengthening El Niño conditions. The Juba River at Dollow is approaching flood level, the Shabelle is near the top of its banks at Jowhar, and heavy rain in Baidoa has already damaged homes; Beledweyne (229,000) and Galkayo (82,000) face the greatest displacement risk.
EVENTS.impl: No-go · Mogadishu AAIA/Halane enclave only, contracted advance. As of 24 October, Laftagareen-aligned Darawish forces still hold Berdale, Dinsoor, Buurhakaba, Qansaxdheere and Awdiinle after their 15–17 October sweep through Bay region, leaving Baidoa as the only major town under the federally backed South West administration, which has announced a counteroffensive starting with Buurhakaba; the Mogadishu–Baidoa road remains cut and a fight for, or negotiated handover of, Baidoa is the base case.

EVENTS.h: Drone-dropped explosives wound six police at Pelaya station in Cesar
EVENTS.s: At least six police officers were wounded early on Wednesday when explosives dropped from drones struck the police station in Pelaya, Cesar department, in north-eastern Colombia, police said. The officers were taken to medical centres; police did not detail the severity of their injuries. Authorities are investigating who carried out the attack in an area where the ELN guerrilla operates.
EVENTS.impl: Workable with advance · Bogotá/Medellín/Cartagena; no-go rural Cauca, Nariño, Catatumbo, Arauca and southern Cesar; avoid Pan-American Highway south of Cali and overland travel on the Venezuelan border. President de la Espriella's offensive against the ELN and FARC dissidents is escalating on both sides: a 22 October air strike on an ELN camp in El Tambo, Cauca killed nine guerrillas including regional commander alias Marcos Pacífico (DW, 23 Oct), the fifth bombing of his term, while guerrillas hit back at fixed police positions, wounding six officers in a drone-bomb attack on the Pelaya station in Cesar on 21 October (AP, 21 Oct) after the 12 October car bomb at the El Bordo toll plaza on the Pan-American Highway (AP, 12 Oct).

EVENTS.h: Slovakia to resume intergovernmental talks with Russia in Moscow on 26 October
EVENTS.s: The Slovak Foreign Ministry said the Russian-Slovak intergovernmental commission for economic, scientific and technical cooperation will meet in Moscow on 26 October, the first session since Russia's 2022 invasion of Ukraine. The agenda centres on energy, including gas and continued oil supplies and nuclear power, plus farming, environment, sport and culture. Slovakia is meant to end Russian gas purchases by late 2027 under EU plans.
EVENTS.impl: Monitored · routine. No terrorism, sabotage, violent protest or transport disruption was confirmed in Slovakia between 10 and 24 October.

EVENTS.h: Zelensky visits Storting, meets parliamentary leaders after Oslo talks
EVENTS.s: President Zelensky visited the Storting on 21 October for meetings with its President Masud Gharahkhani, the parliamentary leaders and the chair of the Foreign Affairs and Defence Committee. The visit followed the previous day's Oslo talks hosted by Støre and Stubb with US envoys Witkoff and Kushner.
EVENTS.impl: Monitored · heightened hybrid vigilance. Norway remains a low-risk operating environment: the only in-window events affecting movement were the heavily policed 20 October Oslo talks between Zelensky, Witkoff, Støre and Stubb and Zelensky's 21 October Storting visit, both of which passed without incident, and the one domestic security operation was Økokrim's 14 October arrest of five people in the Bergen area over fraud and bribery on NATO ship-supply contracts.

EVENTS.h: Istanbul prosecutors order detention of 31 suspects in investment-fund probe
EVENTS.s: The Istanbul chief prosecutor's office on 21 October ordered the detention of 31 suspects in an investigation into share transactions in four listed companies, with 26 in custody by the time of reporting. The probe follows complaints from the Capital Markets Board and is part of a wider investigation into Turkey's investment-fund sector, in which dozens of funds were ordered liquidated last month.
EVENTS.impl: Workable · monitor protests, political flashpoints and flood disruption. No terrorist attack or mass-casualty security incident was recorded in Türkiye between 10 and 24 October; the operational picture is dominated by the aftermath of the 14 October Istanbul flood disaster (eight dead per AFP on 19 October) and by the political crackdown, with the Halk TV seizure on 14 October, continuing detentions of opposition-run municipal officials, and Reuters-reported detention orders for 31 suspects in the investment-fund probe on 21 October.

EVENTS.h: Eritrea restates defensive posture, denies invasion claims and blames Addis for instability
EVENTS.s: Eritrea's Ministry of Foreign Affairs issued a statement on 21 October titled 'Eritrea's Principled Position Regarding the Ongoing Situation with Ethiopia', describing the inviolability of its sovereign boundary as a principle on which every African border depends. The statement accused Ethiopia's ruling Prosperity Party of coveting Eritrea's coast as 'strategically necessary' and set out a framework for regional peace based on non-interference and adherence to international law. A day earlier Information Minister Yemane Gebremeskel dismissed as 'lies' a Tigray Peace Force commander's claim that TPLF leaders had crossed into Eritrea.
EVENTS.impl: Avoid · war-risk border state. Eritrea remains a party to the Tigray confrontation in all but name: Ethiopia told the UN Security Council on 9 October that Eritrean forces had advanced up to 60 km into Tigray, Asmara asked the Council for Chapter VII measures on 10 October, Abiy warned on 19 October of 'very, very, very severe consequences' if Eritrea ignores his calls, and Asmara's 21 October foreign ministry statement restated a purely defensive posture, denied any invasion and accused Ethiopia's ruling party of coveting its coast.

EVENTS.h: Nigeria's imported Ebola case genetically linked to Kenya strain; contacts quarantined
EVENTS.s: Nigeria confirmed its first Ebola case in more than a decade on 20 October, a Ugandan-born woman married to a Swiss diplomat who arrived in Abuja in early October and was not tested until 13 days after falling ill. On 23 October health minister Muhammad Ali Pate said genomic analysis shows the virus is closely related to the strain in Kenya's index case and that contacts are being traced, quarantined and tested, with some results negative and others pending. The Bundibugyo strain has no approved vaccine or treatment; heightened screening is in place at Nigerian airports.
EVENTS.impl: Workable with advance · North-east, Zamfara and Kaduna corridor no-go · Abuja Ebola watch. Between 10 and 24 October the north-east recorded its heaviest military losses in years: ISWAP/Boko Haram overran the Guzamala-Mairari base on 13-14 October (Reuters: at least 10 soldiers, five civilians and a forest guard; AFP sources: 15 soldiers and five CJTF) and a mine-and-ambush on a patrol near Gamboru Ngala on 17 October killed 10 soldiers and five CJTF (Reuters, 19 Oct), while in the north-west bandits killed at least 20 in a military-escorted traders' convoy in Bukkuyum, Zamfara, on 10 October (Reuters, 12 Oct), so armed escort is not sufficient mitigation on rural roads.

EVENTS.h: Gunmen ambush two escorted passenger buses near Agadez, killing at least 11
EVENTS.s: Gunmen aboard three vehicles attacked two buses that had left the mining town of Arlit on the morning of 20 October, about 35 km from Agadez, killing at least 11 passengers and wounding several more, local broadcaster Tegades TV reported and an Agadez resident confirmed to AFP. Soldiers escorting the convoy exchanged fire with the attackers; the Agadez regional governor later put the toll at 12, including a soldier, and convened an emergency security council on 21 October. Niger's arid north is a trafficking corridor and has seen violence linked to wildcat gold mining.
EVENTS.impl: No-go · essential travel only with state-level clearance. The deadliest incident between 10 and 24 October hit the north rather than the jihadist-hit west: gunmen in three vehicles ambushed two escorted passenger buses on the Arlit-Agadez road on 20 October, killing at least 11 (AFP; the Agadez governor later put the toll at 12 including a soldier), on the only corridor used by mining and humanitarian traffic to the uranium belt, and the military escort aboard did not prevent it.

EVENTS.h: Two re-arrested under National Security Act for assisting Iranian intelligence
EVENTS.s: Counter Terrorism Policing re-arrested a 24-year-old British national and a 25-year-old British-Iranian dual national on 20 October on suspicion of assisting a foreign intelligence service, as part of the investigation into activity near RAF Fairford on 27 September. Seven men had earlier been arrested and bailed. The head of counter-terrorism policing said Iranian state involvement is considered highly likely.
EVENTS.impl: Monitored · elevated state-threat activity. The UK picture through 24 October remains dominated by state threats rather than street disorder: the two men re-arrested on 20 October under the National Security Act for assisting Iranian intelligence in the RAF Fairford investigation can be held until 27 October, MI5 said on 13 October that Iran and Russia are both expanding hybrid campaigns, and the Home Secretary set out new sanctions and powers on 12 October.

EVENTS.h: Cabinet sends 500 troops to Milan and creates violent-protest offence
EVENTS.s: The Italian cabinet approved a decree on 20 October deploying an additional 500 soldiers to Milan through the end of the year, creating a new offence of violent participation in a demonstration punishable by up to five years in prison and a fine of up to 20,000 euros, and making parents liable for damage caused by minors. Police said about 2,000 youths took part in the Milan riots on 17 October and more than 100 officers were injured over two days. Parliament must convert the decree within 60 days.
EVENTS.impl: Workable with advance · avoid city-centre protest zones. Italy enters Saturday 24 October with security forces deploying massively for cost-of-living protests planned in eight cities including Rome and Milan, where 500 soldiers patrol under the 20 October decree that also created a violent-protest offence after the 17-18 October riots in Milan, Turin, Bologna, Brescia and Bergamo.

EVENTS.h: Tanker struck by unknown projectile 30 nautical miles south-east of Al Faw
EVENTS.s: UK Maritime Trade Operations said the master of a tanker reported being struck by an unknown projectile about 30 nautical miles south-east of Al Faw, Iraq, at 1830 UTC on 20 October. The crew were reported safe with no reported damage or environmental impact. Vessels were advised to transit with caution while authorities investigate; further tanker strikes were reported off Oman on 21 and 22 October.
EVENTS.impl: Restricted · essential travel with advance, Erbil under drone threat. The Kurdistan Region remains the most active theatre: a missile was fired at an Iranian Kurdish opposition camp north-east of Erbil on 21 October (Reuters), the latest in a series of Iranian strikes on exile camps on 8, 12 and 17 October, and Tehran's ambassador said on 20 October that Baghdad had agreed to expel or hand over the opposition groups (AFP), a claim absent from the Iraqi statement and rejected by the groups themselves.

EVENTS.h: UAE drone strike on al-Shabaab bomb team in Puntland, first in a year
EVENTS.s: Security officials told AFP on 21 October that UAE drones launched from Bosaso airport struck four al-Shabaab militants planting roadside bombs in the Galgala mountain pass on Tuesday 20 October, wounding two, after which Puntland paramilitaries moved in and killed the two insurgents. It was the first reported Emirati strike in Somalia since November 2025 and followed an al-Shabaab explosive attack on Puntland forces; officials said Puntland is expected to announce a fresh offensive against the group in the coming days. The federal government did not comment.
EVENTS.impl: No-go · Mogadishu AAIA/Halane enclave only, contracted advance. As of 24 October, Laftagareen-aligned Darawish forces still hold Berdale, Dinsoor, Buurhakaba, Qansaxdheere and Awdiinle after their 15–17 October sweep through Bay region, leaving Baidoa as the only major town under the federally backed South West administration, which has announced a counteroffensive starting with Buurhakaba; the Mogadishu–Baidoa road remains cut and a fight for, or negotiated handover of, Baidoa is the base case.

EVENTS.h: Zelensky meets Witkoff, Støre and Stubb in Oslo under heavy security
EVENTS.s: Ukrainian President Zelensky held talks in Oslo on 20 October with US envoy Steve Witkoff, hosted by Prime Minister Støre and Finnish President Stubb, with Jared Kushner joining by video. The meeting sought to repair US-Ukraine relations and passed without incident.
EVENTS.impl: Monitored · heightened hybrid vigilance. Norway remains a low-risk operating environment: the only in-window events affecting movement were the heavily policed 20 October Oslo talks between Zelensky, Witkoff, Støre and Stubb and Zelensky's 21 October Storting visit, both of which passed without incident, and the one domestic security operation was Økokrim's 14 October arrest of five people in the Bergen area over fraud and bribery on NATO ship-supply contracts.

EVENTS.h: Sudanese drone strike on Abyei's Amiet market kills at least 153, authorities say
EVENTS.s: Drones struck Amiet market north of Abyei town at about 11:00 on 19 October, hitting a fuel depot and starting fires that were still burning a day later. Abyei's caretaker information minister Yohana Akol Ngor told Reuters the toll had risen from 73 to 153 and could climb further; South Sudan's foreign ministry blamed Sudan's army and summoned its ambassador, and Sudan's foreign ministry denied on 22 October that its forces were involved. UNISFA's verified count on 22 October stood at at least 80 killed with many still missing; MSF treated more than 20 wounded at Ameth Bek hospital.
EVENTS.impl: No-go outside Juba · essential travel only. South Sudan is absorbing direct spillover from Sudan's drone war: the 19 October strike on Amiet market and Todach in Abyei killed at least 80 by UNISFA's verified count on 22 October and 153 by the Abyei administration's figure given to Reuters, with many still missing; the UN Security Council condemned the attack in the strongest terms on 23 October, demanded an investigation and reaffirmed Abyei's demilitarised status, while Khartoum denied on 22 October that its armed forces were involved after Juba summoned Sudan's ambassador.

EVENTS.h: Storm Adam floods eastern Spain: four dead, more than 2,000 evacuated
EVENTS.s: Torrential rain from Storm Adam killed four people, two in Oliva, one at a beach in Sagunto and one swept into a stream in Catalonia, and triggered helicopter rescues of residents from rooftops in southern Valencia and northern Alicante. Pego recorded 632 mm of rain in 36 hours; about 800,000 residents were under shelter-in-place orders on the morning of 19 October, falling to 87,000 in eight municipalities by late afternoon. More than 2,000 people were evacuated, mainly in Oliva, and more than 400 rescues were carried out in the Valencia region.
EVENTS.src: Al Jazeera with AFP and Reuters, 20 Oct 2026
EVENTS.impl: Workable with advance · election-campaign protest watch. Spain's picture shifted from weather to politics in the final days of the window: Storm Adam's floods in the Valencia region and Catalonia on 17-19 October killed four, with clean-up in Oliva, Pego and the Marina Alta still disrupting secondary roads, but on 21 October the first pre-campaign rally by Vox leader Santiago Abascal in A Coruña drew about 5,000 counter-protesters and ended in police charges, rubber bullets, burning bins, around a dozen injured and arrests, with a second night of clashes on 22 October, the first violent spill-over of the European unrest wave into Spain.

EVENTS.h: HRW: Malian army and Africa Corps drone strikes killed scores of civilians
EVENTS.s: Human Rights Watch said on 19 October that Malian forces and Russia's Africa Corps used apparent indiscriminate drone strikes in their offensive since April. Documented cases include a strike on a cattle market in Bandiagara and a 29 July strike on a health centre in Kidal region. The report also documented the execution of 19 captured soldiers by JNIM and FLA fighters in Gao region in July.
EVENTS.impl: No-go · active conflict. Mali remains in open, multi-front war as of 24 October: JNIM has held the Bamako approaches under a fuel blockade since late April, with fuel reaching the capital only in large escorted tanker convoys, while Islamic State Sahel Province's killing of at least 48 civilians (AFP sources: 40 to more than 50; Reuters sources: up to 70+) in Daoussahak camps around Tinabow and Tagadayat in Menaka on 18-19 October, described by Reuters' sources as reprisal for killings of suspected informants by the MSA militia and Africa Corps, marks an escalation in the east even as ISSP and JNIM fight each other across the Burkina border; the army said on 19 October it struck a major ISSP base 65 km south-west of Menaka (AP).

EVENTS.h: RSF drones hit Khartoum airport district killing four; army strike on Nyala kills 17
EVENTS.s: A drone strike on a house in the Nasser Extension neighbourhood east of Khartoum airport on the morning of 19 October killed four people including three children aged two to six, a medical source said; the army said air defences intercepted RSF drones targeting the airport and the Atbara and Setit dams in Gadaref state. Hours earlier an army drone strike on central Nyala, the RSF-held capital of South Darfur, killed 17 people including seven RSF officers and wounded 23, medical and RSF sources said.
EVENTS.impl: No-go · active conflict. Sudan's war is in a drone-dominated phase: the UN Human Rights Office said on 23 October it had documented at least 306 deaths from drone strikes by both sides in the first three weeks of October alone, including a double-tap strike on a transport hub at Dibab in West Kordofan on 18 October that it now puts at 139 dead, army strikes on Nyala and RSF retaliation on Khartoum including the airport district on 19 October, and the 19 October strike on Abyei's Amiet market across the South Sudan border, which Khartoum denied on 22 October.

EVENTS.h: Polish-Ukrainian reservist on officer course detained on spying suspicion
EVENTS.s: Polish military police said on 19 October they had detained a 31-year-old Polish-Ukrainian dual national suspected of spying who was attending an officer training course for reservists in Łódź; the detention took place on 16 October. The case follows a series of Russian-attributed sabotage and espionage incidents in Poland this autumn.
EVENTS.impl: Monitored · hybrid-threat watch. Poland's window was front-loaded: three school stabbings in four days that killed a custodian and triggered checks of nearly 50,000 schools, German arrests announced on 12 October of two Turkish nationals suspected of the Russian-directed Starlink station arson near Warsaw, and the 16 October detention in Łódź, announced 19 October, of a Polish-Ukrainian reservist on an officer course on spying suspicion.

EVENTS.h: Parliament delays vote on military support for Saudi Arabia to 26 October
EVENTS.s: Egypt's parliament delayed until 26 October a vote on authorising the armed forces to support Saudi Arabia if requested, after two emergency sessions on 18 and 19 October failed to reach a vote. The National Defence Council had pledged 'all necessary and possible' support to the kingdom on 18 October. Authorisation requires a two-thirds majority of the 596-member chamber, and the Egyptian Social Democratic Party instructed its lawmakers to abstain citing a lack of detail on the mission's objectives, duration and cost.
EVENTS.impl: Workable · Red Sea/Suez watch; North Sinai and Sudan border restricted. No terrorist attack, Sinai incident or domestic unrest was wire-confirmed in Egypt between 10 and 24 October, but the external-security profile is rising.

EVENTS.h: Malian army says it struck major ISSP base south-west of Menaka
EVENTS.s: The Malian army announced on Monday 19 October that it had located and struck a major base housing several terrorist elements as well as military equipment and logistical supplies 65 km south-west of Menaka town. The statement followed the weekend ISSP attacks on civilians in the region. No casualty figures were given.
EVENTS.impl: No-go · active conflict. Mali remains in open, multi-front war as of 24 October: JNIM has held the Bamako approaches under a fuel blockade since late April, with fuel reaching the capital only in large escorted tanker convoys, while Islamic State Sahel Province's killing of at least 48 civilians (AFP sources: 40 to more than 50; Reuters sources: up to 70+) in Daoussahak camps around Tinabow and Tagadayat in Menaka on 18-19 October, described by Reuters' sources as reprisal for killings of suspected informants by the MSA militia and Africa Corps, marks an escalation in the east even as ISSP and JNIM fight each other across the Burkina border; the army said on 19 October it struck a major ISSP base 65 km south-west of Menaka (AP).

EVENTS.h: Abiy warns Eritrea of 'very severe consequences' if it keeps backing rebels
EVENTS.s: Ethiopian Prime Minister Abiy Ahmed warned on 19 October, in a Tigrinya-language address, that Eritrea faces 'very, very, very severe consequences' if it continues to support rebels in Ethiopia and ignores his calls, while saying he wanted good neighbourly relations. He said the TPLF's existence was 'coming to an end'; Mekelle's new mayor told AFP the caretaker administration would hold elections within six months.
EVENTS.impl: Avoid · war-risk border state. Eritrea remains a party to the Tigray confrontation in all but name: Ethiopia told the UN Security Council on 9 October that Eritrean forces had advanced up to 60 km into Tigray, Asmara asked the Council for Chapter VII measures on 10 October, Abiy warned on 19 October of 'very, very, very severe consequences' if Eritrea ignores his calls, and Asmara's 21 October foreign ministry statement restated a purely defensive posture, denied any invasion and accused Ethiopia's ruling party of coveting its coast.

EVENTS.h: Yemeni refugee arrivals in Obock reach 3,836 as diarrhoea outbreak hits camp
EVENTS.s: UNICEF's 19 October flash update said 3,836 refugees had arrived in Djibouti from Yemen since September according to UNHCR, with children making up 52 percent and 23 new arrivals recorded between 10 and 16 October. An acute watery diarrhoea outbreak in Markazi refugee village had produced 56 cases and three deaths by 17 October, with the first host-community case reported on 14 October. UNHCR's 19 October regional update said no new arrivals from Yemen were reported between 8 and 14 October and that 139 bodies had been recovered from the 8-9 October shipwreck.
EVENTS.impl: Monitored · transit hub. No violent security incident was recorded inside Djibouti between 10 and 24 October; the humanitarian load is the story, with UNHCR counting 3,836 refugees arrived from Yemen in Obock region by 17 October, an acute watery diarrhoea outbreak in the Markazi camp and the aftermath of the 8-9 October migrant shipwreck off Obock (139 dead, 84 missing per IOM), which now falls outside the two-week window.

EVENTS.h: Queimados municipal secretary shot dead by Military Police on Avenida Brasil
EVENTS.s: Jefferson Dias da Silva, 51, Queimados' economic development secretary and a former councillor, was killed on Monday night when officers of the 22nd Military Police Battalion fired on his car during an attempted stop on Avenida Brasil near Bonsucesso. The Military Police opened an internal procedure and the acting state governor ordered the officers involved removed from duty; the Civil Police homicide division is analysing body-camera footage. Two lanes of the artery were closed for the forensic work.
EVENTS.impl: Workable with advance · Rio metro elevated through 25-26 Oct (federal troops in 15 municipalities); avoid favela-adjacent routes and Avenida Brasil at night; expect result-related gatherings in Brasília, São Paulo and Rio on Sunday night and possible court challenges to a narrow result. Brazil votes on Sunday 25 October in a presidential runoff that is a statistical dead heat: Datafolha published a 50-50 tie on 22 October and the final TV Globo debate on 23 October left the share of undecided voters doubling to 14% (AFP, 23 Oct), while each camp has a petition pending at the Superior Electoral Court to disqualify the other, so a narrow result is likely to be contested in court and on the street.

EVENTS.h: New El Mansouri government presents programme targeting 5% growth in 2027-2031
EVENTS.s: Prime Minister Fatima Ezzahra El Mansouri presented her government's five-year programme to parliament on Monday 19 October, targeting average annual growth of 5% between 2027 and 2031. Her four-party coalition, sworn in before King Mohammed VI on 16 October, holds 207 of the 395 seats in the House of Representatives. The programme prioritises anti-corruption measures, social welfare and youth employment after the 2025 GenZ 212 protests over jobs, education and health services.
EVENTS.impl: Monitored · open for business. Morocco recorded no kinetic security incident between 10 and 24 October that a wire service confirmed; the environment remains political and workable nationwide outside the Western Sahara berm zone.

EVENTS.h: Spain's rush to clear Ceuta migrant backlog raises rights concerns
EVENTS.s: Reuters reported that eight charities including Oxfam and Amnesty International filed a complaint with Spain's ombudsman alleging 'grave rights violations' in the Ceuta enclave as Madrid moves to clear the asylum backlog left by the July mass crossing from Morocco. The dispute follows King Mohammed VI's 9 October statement that the migration cooperation model with Spain had reached its limit and the Spanish royals' 13 October visit to Ceuta.
EVENTS.impl: Monitored · open for business. Morocco recorded no kinetic security incident between 10 and 24 October that a wire service confirmed; the environment remains political and workable nationwide outside the Western Sahara berm zone.

EVENTS.h: Largest-ever drone attack on St Petersburg kills one, injures 15, sets oil terminal ablaze
EVENTS.s: One person was killed and 15 injured in a Ukrainian drone attack on oil facilities, logistics and data centres in St Petersburg and the Leningrad region on 18 October, local authorities said. Governor Beglov said fires broke out at the St Petersburg oil terminal, an oil depot and industrial warehouses; Ozon's logistics hub burned and VK's data centre was hit. Russia's Defence Ministry said it downed 1,015 Ukrainian drones overnight.
EVENTS.impl: No-go · active deep-strike campaign and arbitrary detention. Russia's two principal cities remain under sustained Ukrainian drone attack: after the 18 October assault that killed one and injured 15 in St Petersburg and set the oil terminal ablaze, 630 drones were sent towards Moscow overnight on 21-22 October wounding two, and on 23 October a daytime raid forced Rosaviatsia to halt flights at all four Moscow airports and Sheremetyevo to move passengers into shelters, with Mayor Sobyanin reporting 155 drones towards the region overnight and more than 20 downed on approach to the city during the afternoon.

EVENTS.h: ISSP kills at least 48 civilians in Menaka in reprisal over informant killings
EVENTS.s: Islamic State Sahel Province fighters on motorcycles attacked at least five localities in the Menaka region, mainly Daoussahak camps around Tinabow and Tagadayat some 40-50 km from Menaka town, from Sunday night 18 October into Monday morning, killing at least 48 people including children and the elderly, a lawmaker told AP and four Reuters sources said, with provisional tolls ranging up to more than 70. The attackers torched homes and stole livestock, sending hundreds fleeing to Menaka town; the sources said the raids followed abuses the previous week by the pro-government MSA militia and Africa Corps against civilians suspected of informing for Islamic State. ISSP has not claimed responsibility.
EVENTS.impl: No-go · active conflict. Mali remains in open, multi-front war as of 24 October: JNIM has held the Bamako approaches under a fuel blockade since late April, with fuel reaching the capital only in large escorted tanker convoys, while Islamic State Sahel Province's killing of at least 48 civilians (AFP sources: 40 to more than 50; Reuters sources: up to 70+) in Daoussahak camps around Tinabow and Tagadayat in Menaka on 18-19 October, described by Reuters' sources as reprisal for killings of suspected informants by the MSA militia and Africa Corps, marks an escalation in the east even as ISSP and JNIM fight each other across the Burkina border; the army said on 19 October it struck a major ISSP base 65 km south-west of Menaka (AP).

EVENTS.h: Double-tap drone strike on Kordofan transport hub kills at least 80; UN says 139
EVENTS.s: A drone struck twice, ten minutes apart, at a transport hub where villagers were gathering rides home from Al-Dibab market on the evening of 18 October. A medical source told AFP 80 people were killed, including 30 of 47 wounded who died after transfer to Al-Mujlad; the RSF-declared Tasis administration and the Emergency Lawyers group accused the army, which did not comment. The UN Human Rights Office said on 23 October that at least 139 people were killed in the strike.
EVENTS.impl: No-go · active conflict. Sudan's war is in a drone-dominated phase: the UN Human Rights Office said on 23 October it had documented at least 306 deaths from drone strikes by both sides in the first three weeks of October alone, including a double-tap strike on a transport hub at Dibab in West Kordofan on 18 October that it now puts at 139 dead, army strikes on Nyala and RSF retaliation on Khartoum including the airport district on 19 October, and the 19 October strike on Abyei's Amiet market across the South Sudan border, which Khartoum denied on 22 October.

EVENTS.h: Second day of Milan rioting: stones, looting, 271 young people detained
EVENTS.s: Milan police clashed on 18 October with protesters throwing stones and looting shops near Piazza Duomo, firing tear gas and using water cannon after several hundred hooded protesters broke shop windows and set bins on fire. Authorities said 271 young people were detained in Milan on Sunday. A total of 28 protesters were arrested after similar clashes on 17 October in Milan, Bologna, Brescia, Bergamo and Turin.
EVENTS.impl: Workable with advance · avoid city-centre protest zones. Italy enters Saturday 24 October with security forces deploying massively for cost-of-living protests planned in eight cities including Rome and Milan, where 500 soldiers patrol under the 20 October decree that also created a violent-protest offence after the 17-18 October riots in Milan, Turin, Bologna, Brescia and Bergamo.

EVENTS.h: Mortar blast kills at least nine Anti-Threat Security Agency members in Zawiya
EVENTS.s: At least nine members of the Anti-Threat Security Agency, a force under the Tripoli-based Government of National Unity, were killed and several others wounded when an 82mm mortar round exploded during a training exercise in Zawiya late on Sunday 18 October, Libya Alahrar TV reported. Authorities made no immediate comment. Zawiya, about 40 km west of Tripoli and home to the country's largest operating refinery, has been the site of repeated clashes between rival armed groups.
EVENTS.impl: No-go for routine travel · essential only with armed escort and air evacuation plan. Libya remains Critical and the trend is rising: on 22 October individuals entered the AGOCO crude receiving station near the Zawiya refinery and shut the valve on the Hamada-Zawiya pipeline, cutting output at the Hamada and Tahara fields (Reuters) in the second forced pipeline closure in western Libya in five weeks, with no wire-confirmed reopening as of 24 October; on 21 October armed men stormed the National Audit Bureau in Tripoli to impose a disputed deputy head, drawing UNSMIL's strongest condemnation and a warning of targeted sanctions; and on 18 October an 82mm mortar blast killed at least nine Anti-Threat Security Agency personnel during training in Zawiya (Reuters).

EVENTS.h: Two arrested for terrorism in Basque Country over security-force data and suspected arms cache
EVENTS.s: Basque regional police said on 18 October that a 34-year-old Spanish man and a 22-year-old Spanish woman were arrested on suspicion of terrorism offences following a search on 26 September. Items seized included information on security forces and the potential location of a site holding materials presumed to be weapons and explosives. Both will appear before Spain's National Court at a later date.
EVENTS.impl: Workable with advance · election-campaign protest watch. Spain's picture shifted from weather to politics in the final days of the window: Storm Adam's floods in the Valencia region and Catalonia on 17-19 October killed four, with clean-up in Oliva, Pego and the Marina Alta still disrupting secondary roads, but on 21 October the first pre-campaign rally by Vox leader Santiago Abascal in A Coruña drew about 5,000 counter-protesters and ended in police charges, rubber bullets, burning bins, around a dozen injured and arrests, with a second night of clashes on 22 October, the first violent spill-over of the European unrest wave into Spain.

EVENTS.h: Petrol shortage reaches Niamey; night-time fuel sales banned from 19 October
EVENTS.s: Long queues formed at the few supplied stations in Niamey on 18 October after weeks of shortages in other towns, with station managers saying their tanks had been empty for four days, AFP reported. The Commerce Ministry banned petrol and diesel exports by decree on 12 October, and from 19 October the interior, petroleum and commerce ministers prohibited public fuel sales at stations between 21:00 and 06:00 except at designated duty stations (ANP). State oil company Sonidep must import petrol to cover domestic demand.
EVENTS.impl: No-go · essential travel only with state-level clearance. The deadliest incident between 10 and 24 October hit the north rather than the jihadist-hit west: gunmen in three vehicles ambushed two escorted passenger buses on the Arlit-Agadez road on 20 October, killing at least 11 (AFP; the Agadez governor later put the toll at 12 including a soldier), on the only corridor used by mining and humanitarian traffic to the uranium belt, and the military escort aboard did not prevent it.

EVENTS.h: Vehicle breaches Leipzig/Halle airport fence; north runway closed during search
EVENTS.s: German police said on 18 October they were investigating a breach at Leipzig/Halle airport where a vehicle appeared to have driven through a perimeter fence late on 17 October. Searches found no suspicious objects or unauthorised persons, but the north runway remained closed while checks continued. On 19 October police said two men had admitted breaking through the fence while one was practising for a driving test.
EVENTS.impl: Monitored · critical-infrastructure watch. Germany's state-threat environment hardened in the final week of the window: federal prosecutors arrested a Ukrainian national in Brandenburg on 22 October for gathering military intelligence for Russia, including on NATO eastern-flank sites and defence-industry production, one day after the Bundeswehr rated the Russian sabotage threat to its own forces as significant for the first time, and Chancellor Merz said on 22 October that Germany is the target of intensive espionage and more such cases will follow.

EVENTS.h: Nationwide cost-of-living riots: Limoges town hall burned, 3,000 shops hit, 2,400 arrested
EVENTS.s: Huge protests across France over the cost of living and underfunded public services on 17 October descended into riots and looting in some of the worst unrest in years. Limoges town hall was torched and more than 3,000 shops were pillaged or damaged according to the government, as violent groups clashed with police in cities across the country. Some 2,400 people were arrested over the weekend and partial curfews were organised in several municipalities.
EVENTS.impl: Workable with advance · curfew-aware movement planning, avoid protest perimeters. France's risk rose on the eve of the 24 October protest day: a gunman firing an automatic weapon from a car killed one person and seriously wounded four, including a 12-year-old, at three locations in Trappes and La Verrière west of Paris on the morning of 23 October before his arrest in Coignières, and the national anti-terrorism prosecutor opened a murder-in-connection-with-terrorism inquiry with a racial aggravating circumstance, which Macron called a racist terrorist attack.

EVENTS.h: Mine and gunfire on army patrol near Gamboru Ngala kill 10 soldiers, five CJTF
EVENTS.s: Troops from the Gamboru battalion patrolling the road between Gamboru Ngala and Cameroon on Saturday 17 October struck a landmine likely planted by Boko Haram, killing eight soldiers instantly, two soldiers told Reuters. Gunmen then fired on a second vehicle, killing two more soldiers and five Civilian Joint Task Force members. The military spokesperson declined to comment.
EVENTS.impl: Workable with advance · North-east, Zamfara and Kaduna corridor no-go · Abuja Ebola watch. Between 10 and 24 October the north-east recorded its heaviest military losses in years: ISWAP/Boko Haram overran the Guzamala-Mairari base on 13-14 October (Reuters: at least 10 soldiers, five civilians and a forest guard; AFP sources: 15 soldiers and five CJTF) and a mine-and-ambush on a patrol near Gamboru Ngala on 17 October killed 10 soldiers and five CJTF (Reuters, 19 Oct), while in the north-west bandits killed at least 20 in a military-escorted traders' convoy in Bukkuyum, Zamfara, on 10 October (Reuters, 12 Oct), so armed escort is not sufficient mitigation on rural roads.

EVENTS.adm: Bay region (Buurhakaba, Dinsoor, Berdale, Qansaxdheere, Awdiinle)
EVENTS.h: Forces loyal to ousted South West leader seize five Bay towns around Baidoa
EVENTS.s: Military officials said on 17 October that forces loyal to ousted South West State president Abdiaziz Hassan Mohamed Laftagareen had taken Berdale, Dinsoor, Buurhakaba and Qansaxdheere, plus Awdiinle about 30 km from Baidoa, leaving the federally backed administration without control of most of the state. Most takeovers were without resistance, but clashes were reported during the capture of Buurhakaba on the Mogadishu–Baidoa road; local officials fled to an AUSSOM base where Ethiopian troops did not intervene. South West Information Minister Nur Sidow Baba said the districts would be brought back under government control.
EVENTS.impl: No-go · Mogadishu AAIA/Halane enclave only, contracted advance. As of 24 October, Laftagareen-aligned Darawish forces still hold Berdale, Dinsoor, Buurhakaba, Qansaxdheere and Awdiinle after their 15–17 October sweep through Bay region, leaving Baidoa as the only major town under the federally backed South West administration, which has announced a counteroffensive starting with Buurhakaba; the Mogadishu–Baidoa road remains cut and a fight for, or negotiated handover of, Baidoa is the base case.

EVENTS.h: Student protests turn violent in Brussels and Liège; tear gas and water cannon
EVENTS.s: Several hundred mostly young people protested in central Brussels on 17 October against rising education costs, with rioters clashing with police in unrest partly inspired by demonstrations in France. Police used tear gas and water cannon and some protesters overturned a car. Interior Minister Bernard Quintin said what was unfolding was no longer mere protest; a parallel protest took place in Liège.
EVENTS.impl: Workable with advance · strike and protest watch. Belgium remains the most exposed of the smaller core states to the French contagion: union strike days on 9 and 12 October disrupted Brussels Airport, rail, public transport and schools, and student-led protests turned violent in Brussels and Liège on 17 October, with police using tear gas and water cannon.

EVENTS.h: UGTT-led march of thousands is biggest anti-Saied protest in years
EVENTS.s: Thousands of Tunisians joined the largest protest against President Kais Saied in years on Saturday 17 October, led by the UGTT labour union and civil society groups, with hundreds of police deployed across the capital and roads around Habib Bourguiba Avenue closed. Protesters chanted 'The prisons are full, people are hungry!' and revived the 2011 slogan 'The people want the fall of the regime!'. The march passed without reported violence.
EVENTS.impl: Workable · avoid central Tunis, Ettadhamen and Sfax-area flashpoints on protest days. Tunisia's risk profile is rising: on 22 October police fired tear gas at protesters in Ettadhamen, a suburb of Tunis, after the death of a man in custody, with parallel clashes in Jebeniana and Agareb in Sfax governorate and student protests in Sfax city (Reuters), and AFP reported on 23 October that protesters in Ettadhamen burned tyres and blocked roads overnight with no confirmed casualties or arrests, five days after the UGTT-led march of 17 October, the largest show of opposition to President Saied in years.

EVENTS.h: Rubio warns troops surging on both sides of Ethiopia-Eritrea border risk broader conflict
