EVENTS.s: Asked about the risk of war between Eritrea and Ethiopia, US Secretary of State Marco Rubio said on 17 October that troops were surging on both sides of the border following separatist attacks inside Ethiopia and the Ethiopian response, and that this could turn into a broader conflict. He said Washington had more communication than usual with Asmara in recent months and had lifted some small sanctions to improve links so it could act as a mediator.
EVENTS.impl: Avoid · war-risk border state. Eritrea remains a party to the Tigray confrontation in all but name: Ethiopia told the UN Security Council on 9 October that Eritrean forces had advanced up to 60 km into Tigray, Asmara asked the Council for Chapter VII measures on 10 October, Abiy warned on 19 October of 'very, very, very severe consequences' if Eritrea ignores his calls, and Asmara's 21 October foreign ministry statement restated a purely defensive posture, denied any invasion and accused Ethiopia's ruling party of coveting its coast.

EVENTS.h: Opposition wins Senate runoffs; Babiš's ANO takes no seats
EVENTS.s: Leading opposition parties won the most votes in Senate elections on 17 October, while Prime Minister Andrej Babiš's ANO failed to secure any of the seats it contested. The pro-European Mayors and Independents won 10 of the 14 seats they contested and the Civic Democrats seven. Babiš called the result catastrophic, but the outcome is unlikely to destabilise his coalition, which controls the lower house.
EVENTS.impl: Monitored · routine. No terrorism, sabotage, violent unrest or major transport disruption was confirmed in Czechia between 10 and 24 October.

EVENTS.h: Abiy names six-month Tigray caretaker government and calls for elections
EVENTS.s: Prime Minister Abiy Ahmed named a caretaker administration to stabilise Tigray and prepare an election within six months, after the military and a pro-government militia took control of large parts of the region including Mekelle. His office said the administration would also repair infrastructure and help displaced people return; a TPLF spokesperson did not immediately comment. Around 750,000 Tigrayans were still internally displaced as of February, according to UNHCR.
EVENTS.impl: No-go north of Addis · Addis essential travel with advance. Tigray is easing but not settled: federal forces and the allied Tigray Peace Force hold Mekelle, Adigrat, Adwa and Axum, shops and banks were reopening in Mekelle on 22 October and schools are due to resume on 26 October under the six-month caretaker administration Abiy named on 16 October, yet the TPLF rejects it, Abiy warned Eritrea on 19 October of 'very severe consequences' if it keeps backing his enemies, and troops face each other along the Eritrean border.

EVENTS.h: EU approves nearly 32 million euros for Estonia's eastern-border drone surveillance
EVENTS.s: Prime Minister Kristen Michal said at the European Council on 16 October that Estonia will receive nearly 32 million euros from the EU to strengthen drone surveillance along its eastern border. EU leaders also highlighted the Eastern Flank Watch project and agreed to restrict tourist visas for Russian nationals and step up sanctions pressure.
EVENTS.impl: Workable · do not cross into Russia from Narva. No significant security incident occurred on Estonian territory between 10 and 24 October 2026; in-window reporting is dominated by deterrence and resilience measures, including Foreign Minister Tsahkna's 15 October warning that Russia will intensify hybrid attacks and the nearly 32 million euros in EU funding confirmed on 16 October for eastern-border drone surveillance.

EVENTS.h: Kinshasa bans 13 parties including Kabila's PPRD, calls FRN 'attack'
EVENTS.s: Interior Minister Jacquemain Shabani ordered a nationwide ban on the activities of 13 political parties, including Kabila's PPRD, three days after the FRN launch. Government spokesman Patrick Muyaya said Kabila had formalised his attack against the Republic and that taking up arms meant killing Congolese to conquer territory. Opposition figures called the ban repression; the measure gives no duration or legal basis.
EVENTS.impl: No-go · east (Kivus, Ituri) active conflict; Kinshasa workable with advance. Rating held at 4.

EVENTS.h: EU grants Finland 32 million euros for Border Guard drone detection and counter-drone systems
EVENTS.s: The Ministry of the Interior announced on 15 October that Finland will receive 32 million euros from the EU Border Management and Visa Instrument to buy drone surveillance and counter-drone systems for the Border Guard. The systems are to improve drone monitoring on the eastern border and in the Gulf of Finland, with most procurements planned for 2027-2029.
EVENTS.src: Finnish Ministry of the Interior, 15 Oct 2026
EVENTS.impl: Workable · avoid SE border zone during Russia strike nights. Finland is safe for travel and operations, but the south-eastern coast between Loviisa and the Russian border is subject to short-notice air and sea closures whenever Ukraine mounts large strikes on St Petersburg; the Defence Forces imposed such restrictions on three consecutive mornings on 16, 17 and 18 October with no drones crossing into Finland, and no new restrictions were reported on 22-24 October.

EVENTS.h: Tsahkna warns Russia will step up hybrid attacks to erode Western support for Ukraine
EVENTS.s: Foreign Minister Margus Tsahkna told Reuters at the Warsaw Security Forum on 15 October that the risk of Russia eroding Western support for Ukraine through hybrid attacks, sabotage and disinformation is a key concern for Estonia. European officials have warned that Moscow is intensifying such operations against NATO states.
EVENTS.impl: Workable · do not cross into Russia from Narva. No significant security incident occurred on Estonian territory between 10 and 24 October 2026; in-window reporting is dominated by deterrence and resilience measures, including Foreign Minister Tsahkna's 15 October warning that Russia will intensify hybrid attacks and the nearly 32 million euros in EU funding confirmed on 16 October for eastern-border drone surveillance.

EVENTS.h: Istanbul's worst floods in 80 years kill eight, thousands of properties damaged
EVENTS.s: Record rainfall on the night of 14 October flooded homes, businesses and streets across Istanbul in what the interior minister called the biggest flood disaster since 1942. Istanbul governor Davut Gul said on 19 October that six people had died in Istanbul and two in neighbouring Kocaeli, taking the toll to eight with one person still missing; authorities had received nearly 20,000 property-damage reports. The last missing person was found dead in the Golden Horn on 20 October, ending the search.
EVENTS.impl: Workable · monitor protests, political flashpoints and flood disruption. No terrorist attack or mass-casualty security incident was recorded in Türkiye between 10 and 24 October; the operational picture is dominated by the aftermath of the 14 October Istanbul flood disaster (eight dead per AFP on 19 October) and by the political crackdown, with the Halk TV seizure on 14 October, continuing detentions of opposition-run municipal officials, and Reuters-reported detention orders for 31 suspects in the investment-fund probe on 21 October.

EVENTS.h: Roadside bomb kills Iraqi army brigadier and soldier south of Kirkuk
EVENTS.s: A roadside bomb killed an Iraqi army brigadier and a soldier and wounded two other soldiers about 80 km south of Kirkuk on 14 October as a patrol searched an Islamic State hideout struck by warplanes the day before. It was the second attack on security forces in the area this month after a 5 October attack claimed by Islamic State.
EVENTS.impl: Restricted · essential travel with advance, Erbil under drone threat. The Kurdistan Region remains the most active theatre: a missile was fired at an Iranian Kurdish opposition camp north-east of Erbil on 21 October (Reuters), the latest in a series of Iranian strikes on exile camps on 8, 12 and 17 October, and Tehran's ambassador said on 20 October that Baghdad had agreed to expel or hand over the opposition groups (AFP), a claim absent from the Iraqi statement and rejected by the groups themselves.

EVENTS.h: Police raid opposition broadcaster Halk TV as government trustee appointed
EVENTS.s: Turkish authorities appointed a government trustee to run pro-opposition broadcaster Halk TV and police raided its Istanbul office, prosecutors said on 14 October. Live broadcasts were halted as part of an investigation into the channel's owner, extending a crackdown on critical media.
EVENTS.impl: Workable · monitor protests, political flashpoints and flood disruption. No terrorist attack or mass-casualty security incident was recorded in Türkiye between 10 and 24 October; the operational picture is dominated by the aftermath of the 14 October Istanbul flood disaster (eight dead per AFP on 19 October) and by the political crackdown, with the Halk TV seizure on 14 October, continuing detentions of opposition-run municipal officials, and Reuters-reported detention orders for 31 suspects in the investment-fund probe on 21 October.

EVENTS.h: Five arrested in Norway over fraud and bribery on NATO ship contracts
EVENTS.s: Five people were arrested in Norway on 14 October and searches carried out in Germany and Romania in a Eurojust-coordinated probe into fraudulent invoicing and bribery linked to shore-support contracts for NATO vessels. Eurojust estimated losses to NATO member countries at around one million euros; Økokrim said the suspects were held in the Bergen area.
EVENTS.impl: Monitored · heightened hybrid vigilance. Norway remains a low-risk operating environment: the only in-window events affecting movement were the heavily policed 20 October Oslo talks between Zelensky, Witkoff, Støre and Stubb and Zelensky's 21 October Storting visit, both of which passed without incident, and the one domestic security operation was Økokrim's 14 October arrest of five people in the Bergen area over fraud and bribery on NATO ship-supply contracts.

EVENTS.h: US lifts sanctions on Assembly chief Jorge Rodríguez as third round of talks opens
EVENTS.s: The Trump administration removed Jorge Rodríguez, head of the National Assembly and brother of acting President Delcy Rodríguez, from the Treasury sanctions list on Wednesday. The notice came as he opened the third round of US-backed talks with an opposition faction on reforms to the top court and electoral council ahead of eventual elections. Caracas and Washington have a deal giving the US access to 17 oilfields.
EVENTS.impl: Monitored · Caracas workable with advance; stand off from all demonstrations and party marches in central Caracas (Plaza Venezuela, Miraflores approaches), low profile, no overland border travel. The first nationwide opposition protest in nearly two years on 22 October passed without wire-reported violence, with thousands marching in Caracas, Valencia, Maracay, San Cristóbal and Maracaibo for a 2027 election date and the release of political prisoners while the ruling party staged a rival march from the same square (Reuters, 22 Oct); Machado's party afterwards said seven marchers were detained by the Bolivarian National Police (AFP, 23 Oct).

EVENTS.h: Boko Haram/ISWAP overruns Guzamala army base, killing at least 10 soldiers
EVENTS.s: Suspected Boko Haram fighters attacked the army base in Guzamala local government area on the night of Tuesday 13 October, overrunning troops, destroying military vehicles and burning parts of nearby Mairari village, military sources told Reuters. At least 10 soldiers, five civilians and a forest guard were killed and more than 20 wounded; AFP's defence sources put the toll at 15 soldiers and five CJTF members and said the base was razed, forcing troops to withdraw towards Monguno. The fighters seized more than 40 fishing boats before the assault.
EVENTS.impl: Workable with advance · North-east, Zamfara and Kaduna corridor no-go · Abuja Ebola watch. Between 10 and 24 October the north-east recorded its heaviest military losses in years: ISWAP/Boko Haram overran the Guzamala-Mairari base on 13-14 October (Reuters: at least 10 soldiers, five civilians and a forest guard; AFP sources: 15 soldiers and five CJTF) and a mine-and-ambush on a patrol near Gamboru Ngala on 17 October killed 10 soldiers and five CJTF (Reuters, 19 Oct), while in the north-west bandits killed at least 20 in a military-escorted traders' convoy in Bukkuyum, Zamfara, on 10 October (Reuters, 12 Oct), so armed escort is not sufficient mitigation on rural roads.

EVENTS.h: MI5 chief: Iran targeting military sites, Russia 'aggressor number one'
EVENTS.s: MI5 Director General Ken McCallum said in his annual threat update that Iran is attempting to hit harder targets such as military sites and that Iran-linked operations led to more than 50 arrests in the past year, much of the activity aimed at Jewish communities. He called Russia aggressor number one and said state-threat casework has quadrupled in a decade. He said the RAF Fairford incident was not unique.
EVENTS.impl: Monitored · elevated state-threat activity. The UK picture through 24 October remains dominated by state threats rather than street disorder: the two men re-arrested on 20 October under the National Security Act for assisting Iranian intelligence in the RAF Fairford investigation can be held until 27 October, MI5 said on 13 October that Iran and Russia are both expanding hybrid campaigns, and the Home Secretary set out new sanctions and powers on 12 October.

EVENTS.h: Slovakia restores military attachés with Russia for first time since 2022
EVENTS.s: Slovakia has restored military-diplomatic relations with Russia for the first time since the 2022 invasion of Ukraine, sending two military officers to Moscow while a Russian military attaché is expected in Bratislava. Prime Minister Robert Fico agreed the step with Vladimir Putin in the Kremlin in May. The opposition and former senior officers warn of espionage risks and damage to trust within NATO.
EVENTS.impl: Monitored · routine. No terrorism, sabotage, violent protest or transport disruption was confirmed in Slovakia between 10 and 24 October.

EVENTS.h: Ex-president Kabila launches FRN front, absorbing AFC/M23 rebellion
EVENTS.s: Joseph Kabila launched the Front pour la Refondation de la Nation (FRN), a political-military coalition replacing the AFC/M23 alliance, at a press conference at his residence in rebel-held Goma. Rebel leaders Corneille Nangaa, Bertrand Bisimwa, Freddy Kaniki and Sultani Makenga will serve as his deputies, and the group says it will end 'tyranny' by all means including force. Kabila was sentenced to death in absentia last year for treason and is under US sanctions.
EVENTS.impl: No-go · east (Kivus, Ituri) active conflict; Kinshasa workable with advance. Rating held at 4.

EVENTS.h: Second national strike day partly shuts public sector, rail and schools
EVENTS.s: Belgium's public sector was partially shut down on 12 October as unions staged a second day of nationwide strike action against planned budget cuts. Rail, public transport, public broadcasting and schools were affected. The action followed a mass protest in Brussels on 9 October that ended with a small group clashing with police, and came as coalition partners failed to agree a federal budget, forcing De Wever to cancel his State of the Union address.
EVENTS.impl: Workable with advance · strike and protest watch. Belgium remains the most exposed of the smaller core states to the French contagion: union strike days on 9 and 12 October disrupted Brussels Airport, rail, public transport and schools, and student-led protests turned violent in Brussels and Liège on 17 October, with police using tear gas and water cannon.

EVENTS.h: Germany detains two Turkish suspects in Russia-linked Starlink station arson in Poland
EVENTS.s: Prime Minister Donald Tusk said on 12 October that German police, at the request of Polish security services, had detained two Turkish citizens suspected of setting fire to a Starlink ground station in Wola Krobowska on 23 September. Polish officials said the sabotage was carried out on behalf of Russian intelligence and that the suspects will face charges in Poland. The station provides satellite internet to Poland and other countries including Ukraine.
EVENTS.impl: Monitored · hybrid-threat watch. Poland's window was front-loaded: three school stabbings in four days that killed a custodian and triggered checks of nearly 50,000 schools, German arrests announced on 12 October of two Turkish nationals suspected of the Russian-directed Starlink station arson near Warsaw, and the 16 October detention in Łódź, announced 19 October, of a Polish-Ukrainian reservist on an officer course on spying suspicion.

EVENTS.h: Car bomb at El Bordo toll booth on Pan-American Highway injures three civilians
EVENTS.s: A car bomb exploded at a toll booth near El Bordo on Monday, injuring at least three civilians, the army said, blaming the FARC-dissident Carlos Patiño front. The same group killed an army sergeant in a clash in Timbío on Friday 9 October, and an ELN drone attack on a patrol in La Vega killed a soldier on Saturday 10 October. President de la Espriella called the toll-booth blast a terrorist attack on the highway.
EVENTS.impl: Workable with advance · Bogotá/Medellín/Cartagena; no-go rural Cauca, Nariño, Catatumbo, Arauca and southern Cesar; avoid Pan-American Highway south of Cali and overland travel on the Venezuelan border. President de la Espriella's offensive against the ELN and FARC dissidents is escalating on both sides: a 22 October air strike on an ELN camp in El Tambo, Cauca killed nine guerrillas including regional commander alias Marcos Pacífico (DW, 23 Oct), the fifth bombing of his term, while guerrillas hit back at fixed police positions, wounding six officers in a drone-bomb attack on the Pelaya station in Cesar on 21 October (AP, 21 Oct) after the 12 October car bomb at the El Bordo toll plaza on the Pan-American Highway (AP, 12 Oct).

EVENTS.h: Home Secretary announces Iran sanctions, state-threats unit and base security
EVENTS.s: Home Secretary Shabana Mahmood told Parliament the government is sanctioning two individuals involved in espionage and attacks on behalf of Iran in Europe and the US, has designated the IRGC under the National Security (State Threats) Act, and is building a specialist state-threats mission in Counter Terror Policing while tightening security around military bases. She said more than 23 people have been charged under the National Security Act since 2023.
EVENTS.impl: Monitored · elevated state-threat activity. The UK picture through 24 October remains dominated by state threats rather than street disorder: the two men re-arrested on 20 October under the National Security Act for assisting Iranian intelligence in the RAF Fairford investigation can be held until 27 October, MI5 said on 13 October that Iran and Russia are both expanding hybrid campaigns, and the Home Secretary set out new sanctions and powers on 12 October.

EVENTS.h: Vienna prosecutors say journalist's spying arrest was unrelated to his job
EVENTS.s: The Vienna prosecutors' office said on 12 October that investigative journalist Mykhailo Tkach was arrested because witnesses saw him observing the same location as two men suspected of spying, not because of his profession. Tkach and cameraman Yaroslav Bondarenko were released without charge; Bondarenko was injured by glass from a car window during the arrest. The two other Ukrainians remain in investigative custody.
EVENTS.impl: Monitored · routine. Austria's window closed with a counter-intelligence move rather than a security incident: on 23 October the foreign ministry declared four Vienna-based Russian diplomats, three at the embassy and one at the OSCE delegation, personae non gratae for activities incompatible with their status, and Moscow said it would respond.

EVENTS.h: PAM agrees four-party coalition government with Istiqlal, USFP and PPS
EVENTS.s: The centrist Authenticity and Modernity Party, winner of the 23 September election, agreed on Monday 12 October to form a coalition government with three other parties. The parties said the deal 'produces a strong political government, made up of components marked by ideological and political proximity'. The cabinet was subsequently appointed by the King on 16 October.
EVENTS.impl: Monitored · open for business. Morocco recorded no kinetic security incident between 10 and 24 October that a wire service confirmed; the environment remains political and workable nationwide outside the Western Sahara berm zone.

EVENTS.h: Algeria says it arrested 61 Moroccans suspected of preparing 'acts of sabotage'
EVENTS.s: The General Directorate of National Security announced on Sunday 11 October that 61 Moroccan nationals had been arrested earlier in the month on suspicion of planning 'acts of sabotage', referring to 'an international Moroccan criminal network' without detailing the plots. The suspects are said to have entered Algeria via mountain trails from Tunisia. The land border with Morocco has been closed since 1994 and diplomatic relations were severed in 2021.
EVENTS.impl: Workable with advance · southern and eastern border zones restricted. No terrorist attack, clash or significant protest was wire-confirmed in Algeria between 10 and 24 October; the environment is stable but heavily securitised and the state continues to frame domestic problems as foreign-backed subversion.

EVENTS.h: Air strikes on Sudan-border gold mine kill at least 72, rights group says
EVENTS.s: At least 72 workers were killed in air strikes on the Jabal al-Uqaydat gold mine on the Sudan-Egypt border on Saturday 10 October, Sudan's Emergency Lawyers rights group said on 11 October, accusing the Egyptian air force; AFP could not independently verify the account and Egypt issued no comment, while AP initially reported at least 13 miners killed and 28 wounded. Survivors told AFP a jet struck five times at around 8am with thousands of people at the site. It was the second strike this year on the site after one in June that killed 23, which the Egyptian army said was an operation 'within Egyptian territory' against illegal gold mining and arms smuggling.
EVENTS.impl: Workable · Red Sea/Suez watch; North Sinai and Sudan border restricted. No terrorist attack, Sinai incident or domestic unrest was wire-confirmed in Egypt between 10 and 24 October, but the external-security profile is rising.

EVENTS.h: Third school attack in a week; custodian killed earlier, 76 detained in nationwide sweep
EVENTS.s: A 21-year-old woman wounded three people with a dangerous object at a post-secondary school in Warsaw's Praga district on 10 October, the third attack at a Polish school in less than a week; none of the injuries was life-threatening. On 7 October a 19-year-old injured nine people at a vocational school in Masovia and on 8 October a 15-year-old killed a school custodian and wounded two others at his former school. Police said they detained 76 people and checked nearly 50,000 schools nationwide to prevent further violence.
EVENTS.impl: Monitored · hybrid-threat watch. Poland's window was front-loaded: three school stabbings in four days that killed a custodian and triggered checks of nearly 50,000 schools, German arrests announced on 12 October of two Turkish nationals suspected of the Russian-directed Starlink station arson near Warsaw, and the 16 October detention in Łódź, announced 19 October, of a Polish-Ukrainian reservist on an officer course on spying suspicion.

ADVS.t: Nigeria — first Ebola case in Abuja: screening and evacuation cover
ADVS.b: Current as of 24 October 2026. Nigeria confirmed its first Ebola case in more than a decade on 20 October: a Ugandan-born woman who arrived in Abuja in early October, fell ill and was treated at a private hospital before being tested (Reuters, AP, DW); on 21 October the NCDC confirmed the Bundibugyo strain, on 22 October the health minister said there was no evidence of community spread, and on 23 October he said genomic analysis links the virus closely to the strain in Kenya's index case, with contacts quarantined and tested, some negative and others pending (Reuters, 23 Oct). The NCDC begins daily public updates on 24 October; there is no approved vaccine or treatment for this species, and the wider outbreak stood at 9,765 cases and 4,727 deaths on 23 October (UN News). No travel restrictions are in force, heightened screening is in place at Nigerian airports, and the security picture in Abuja and Lagos is unchanged.
pts: Confirm medical-evacuation cover and the receiving facility for every principal in Abuja and Lagos before travel; private hospitals in Abuja are the exposure point so far
Brief principals on symptom reporting and avoiding non-essential clinic visits; carry a 72-hour medical kit
Expect entry screening and possible route changes at Nnamdi Azikiwe and Murtala Muhammed airports; build slack into transfers
Trigger for posture review: any secondary case, a healthcare-worker infection, or a case outside Abuja

ADVS.t: Western Europe — protest, curfew and strike disruption (France, Italy, Belgium)
ADVS.b: Current as of 24 October 2026. France enters its second protest Saturday with 70,000 security personnel deployed (20% more than on 17 October), all demonstrations banned in Lyon, Nice and Montpellier, Paris marches confined to a Bastille–Nation route, curfews extended in Marseille and the Louvre and other major Paris museums closed (France 24/AFP, 23 Oct); courts have jailed 217 people over the 17 October riots and student groups meeting Macron on 23 October vowed to keep mobilising. Separately, a gunman firing from a car killed one and wounded four, including a child, in Trappes and La Verrière west of Paris on the morning of 23 October before his arrest; the national anti-terrorism prosecutor opened a racially aggravated terrorism inquiry and Macron called it a racist terrorist attack (France 24/AFP, 23 Oct) — expect heightened policing and the risk of reactive gatherings in the western suburbs. Milan saw two days of rioting and looting (271 detained), a 20 October cabinet decree sends 500 troops to the city to year-end and rallies are called for 24 October in Milan, Florence, Bologna, Turin, Rome and Naples; Belgian education and budget protests turned violent in Brussels and Liège on 17 October, budget talks failed again on 21 October and a deal is now expected next week. Haulier blockades that emptied shelves and pumps in southern Italy began to lift in Sicily and Calabria on 22 October after the cabinet approved a diesel-aid decree (Reuters, 22 Oct); confirm fuel and road status before routing through Campania and Calabria.
pts: Check curfew hours and protest calendars before any evening movement in Paris, Milan, Turin, Rome or Brussels
Pre-book ground transport and build a 24-hour slip into itineraries through Brussels and Italian hubs on announced strike days
Screen venue-adjacent accommodation for protest-zone exposure; avoid city-centre squares on announced march days
Fuel: full tanks before entering southern Italy until roadblocks are fully cleared; confirm aviation-fuel status before booking into Calabrian regional airports

ADVS.b: Current as of 24 October 2026. Al-Shabaab activity in the capital is at its lowest level in years and is now low-lethality harassment of checkpoints on the western (Afgooye-corridor) districts, mostly overnight; no large or complex attack in Mogadishu or at the airport was wire-reported between 10 and 24 October. The threats that reach the airport enclave are different: indirect fire — seven mortar barrages on AAIA and Halane between January 2024 and May 2025, one of them lethal, none since — and government–opposition confrontation, which reached the AAIA perimeter in June 2026 and is building again: the federal government has lost most of South West State to forces loyal to the ousted regional president, who hold Buurhakaba on the Mogadishu–Baidoa road (AFP, 17 Oct), and set a contested April–May 2027 election timetable that Puntland, Jubaland and the opposition reject (AFP/Reuters, 15 Oct); the South West administration has announced a counteroffensive starting with Buurhakaba, so the Mogadishu–Baidoa road should be treated as cut. In the north, a UAE drone strike in the Galgala pass on 20 October — the first in almost a year — precedes an expected new Puntland offensive against al-Shabaab (AFP, 21 Oct).
pts: Movement limited to the AAIA/Halane enclave and the airport road, with contracted armed advance; no movement into Hodan, Daynile or the Afgooye corridor
Indirect-fire drills and hard cover current for every principal in the enclave; last barrage cadence was four in nine weeks (Apr–May 2025)
In-place plan that does not depend on the airport road being open, with 72 hours of self-sufficiency
Trigger for posture review: armed convoys entering Wadajir or Waaberi, security forces surrounding opposition residences, or any mortar fire anywhere in Banaadir
Sanctions screening re-run on any counterparty with South West State or Laftagareen links

ADVS.b: Current as of 24 October 2026. Mali (ISSP killing of at least 48 civilians in Ménaka, 18–19 Oct), Niger (gunmen killed at least 11 — 12 by the governor's later count — on two escorted passenger buses outside Agadez, 20 Oct), Sudan (the UN Human Rights Office documented at least 306 drone-strike deaths in the first three weeks of October, putting the 18 Oct West Kordofan transport-hub strike at 139 dead; army strike on Nyala killed 17 on 19 Oct — OHCHR, 23 Oct; AP, 19 Oct), South Sudan (Abyei's Amiet market strike of 19 Oct: at least 80 killed by UNISFA's verified count, 153 by the Abyei administration's; condemned by the UN Security Council on 23 Oct), northern Ethiopia and Eritrea (federal–TPLF settlement contested, troops facing each other at Zalambessa, Abiy warning Asmara of 'very severe consequences' on 19 Oct, and Oromia–Somali regional fighting at Moyale since 21 Oct killing at least nine and pushing at least 2,500 people into Kenya — Reuters, 23 Oct) and eastern DRC remain outside the TCG movement envelope. Requirements in these jurisdictions are referred, not accepted, unless a dedicated advance and armed local capability are contracted in writing.
pts: No principal movement without contracted local armed support
Written client acknowledgement of residual risk before mobilisation
Medical evacuation route confirmed and funded before deployment — Djibouti and Nairobi remain the staging assumption
Sanctions screening on every local counterparty

ADVS.t: Kurdistan Region — drone threat to Erbil and flight contingency
ADVS.b: Current as of 24 October 2026. Four Iranian strikes in two weeks on Iranian Kurdish opposition sites in Erbil province — drones on 8, 12 and 17 Oct, and a missile at a camp north-east of the city on 21 Oct (Reuters) — plus an explosion at a PMF headquarters in Baghdad (17 Oct) and Iraq's closure of the Sheeb crossing with Iran for a security review (21 Oct). Tehran says Baghdad has agreed to expel or hand over the opposition groups (AFP, 20 Oct); no further strike was wire-reported on 22–24 Oct. Offshore, a tanker was struck by an unknown projectile 30 nautical miles south-east of Al Faw on 20 Oct with no casualties (UKMTO), and further tanker strikes were reported off Oman on 21–22 Oct. With coalition air defences gone since the 30 September US withdrawal, commercial schedules into Erbil remain exposed to short-notice airspace closures.
pts: Build a 24-hour slip into inbound itineraries
Confirm ground assets independently of flight status
Avoid the western and north-eastern approaches to Erbil (Koya, Zrgwez and Balisan camp areas) where strikes have landed
Brief principals on overland alternatives via Türkiye before departure

ADVS.t: Russia and the Baltic–Nordic frontier — hybrid and deep-strike exposure
ADVS.b: Current as of 24 October 2026. Russia: largest drone attack yet on St Petersburg (18 Oct, one killed, oil terminal ablaze), 630 drones sent towards Moscow overnight on 21–22 Oct with apartment blocks hit in Lipetsk (Reuters), and on 23 Oct a daytime raid forced Rosaviatsia to halt flights at all four Moscow airports for the second time in a week, with Sheremetyevo passengers moved into shelters and Mayor Sobyanin reporting 155 drones overnight and more than 20 downed on approach during the afternoon (mos.ru, 23 Oct). A Swedish national was arrested by the FSB on sabotage charges (15 Oct) — detention risk for Western nationals is arbitrary, and the 21 Oct release of American Stephen Hubbard during the Witkoff talks shows detainees are traded as diplomatic currency. Finland closed Gulf of Finland air and sea zones on Russian strike nights (16 and 18 Oct) and took government public web services offline on 21 Oct over critical PHP flaws (BBC); an Estonian ex-soldier is held by the FSB after crossing from Narva.
pts: Russia is no-go for TCG principals; no overland crossings from Narva or the Finnish south-east
Expect short-notice closures of Finnish and Estonian coastal airspace on Russian strike nights
Treat GPS degradation as standard in the Gulf of Finland and eastern Baltic
Brief dual nationals and anyone with prior military service on arbitrary-detention exposure

ADVS.t: Kenya — Ebola screening and Level 3 advisory
ADVS.b: Current as of 24 October 2026. The United States raised Kenya to Level 3 (reconsider travel) on 19 October over Ebola, crime and terrorism; on 23 October the health ministry announced a second Ebola death, a 65-year-old relative of the index patient who fell ill in quarantine, in a nine-case cluster that still shows no transmission outside the family and healthcare-worker group (DW/Reuters/AFP, 23 Oct). Also on 23 October an 18-storey building under construction collapsed in Eastleigh, Nairobi, with seven people reported missing and police firing tear gas at looters (AFP) — avoid the 9th Street area while search and rescue continues. In the north, fighting between Ethiopia's Oromia and Somali regional forces in Moyale since 21 October has killed at least nine, pushed at least 2,500 Ethiopians into Marsabit county and sent stray rounds into the Kenyan town (Reuters, 23 Oct), and a Special Operations Group raid near the Somali border killed 11 al-Shabaab fighters said to be preparing an attack in Mandera (Kenya News Agency, 21 Oct). Nairobi remains the regional hub and staging node.
pts: Health screening and medical-evacuation cover confirmed for every principal transiting Nairobi
No movement into Garissa, Mandera, Wajir or Lamu counties, or to Moyale and the Marsabit border strip while the Ethiopian fighting continues
Brief principals against unvetted ride-hailing and after-dark solo movement in Nairobi

OUTLOOK.a: Core Europe faces a 90-day period in which two threat streams run in parallel: a youth- and cost-of-living-driven unrest wave that has produced the worst French street violence in years, riots in Milan, violent protests in Brussels and A Coruña and a racially aggravated terror shooting outside Paris, and a Russian hybrid campaign that Germany's armed forces now rate a significant sabotage threat, with spy arrests in Brandenburg and Łódź and four Russian diplomats expelled from Vienna in a single week. Electoral calendars will keep the first stream hot: Spain votes on 29 November with a general strike on 11 November, Belgium's budget deadlock carries a late-November general-strike mandate, Italy must convert its protest decree within 60 days, and France is six months from a presidential election with the far right leading polls. Expect recurrent Saturday protest days with curfews and bans in France and Italy through November, spill-over to Belgium and Spain, and further sabotage or espionage cases in Germany and Poland before Christmas, without a change in the baseline for routine business travel to the UK, Czechia, Slovakia and Austria.
dr: Cost-of-living and education-funding protests organised on social media that outrun police intelligence and attract looting fringes, now with a terrorism dimension after Trappes.
Russian hybrid operations against defence, transport and satellite infrastructure on NATO's eastern flank, with Germany, Poland and Austria all taking counter-intelligence action in the same week.
Pre-election polarisation in Spain, France and Italy, including far-right rallies and congresses that draw violent counter-protest, plus unresolved budget fights in Belgium.
ind: Outcome of the 24 October protest day in France and Italy: arrest totals, looting and whether curfews and bans are extended into November.
Belgian budget deal or collapse and any FGTB general-strike date; Spanish 11 November general strike and campaign-rally violence before 29 November.
New sabotage, drone or arson incidents at German, Polish or Czech military, rail or airport sites, and Russia's retaliation for the Austrian expulsions.
OUTLOOK.im: Journey managers should treat Saturdays in French and Italian city centres as no-move windows until the protest cycle breaks, build curfew and protest-ban perimeters into itineraries, and keep fuel and regional-airport contingencies for southern Italy; for Germany and Poland, brief travellers on heightened security at airports and near military sites rather than restricting travel.

OUTLOOK.a: Over the next 90 days the Nordic-Baltic states will stay low-to-moderate risk while Russia remains no-go: Ukraine's deep-strike campaign against St Petersburg and Moscow is intensifying rather than abating, so Finland's south-eastern airspace and sea closures and Baltic stray-drone alerts will recur on strike nights through the winter. Russian hybrid activity against NATO's northern flank (sabotage, cyber, GNSS jamming, espionage) is expected to continue at the current tempo, with the EU moving to restrict Russian tourist visas in response, but no conventional military threat to Norway, Finland or Estonia is anticipated. The US-brokered track (Witkoff-Putin talks, the Oleshky truce and planned Abu Dhabi meetings in early November) could reduce strike intensity if it produces a wider ceasefire, but the pattern of talks followed by record barrages argues for planning on continued disruption.
dr: Ukrainian long-range drone campaign against St Petersburg, Moscow and Leningrad-region energy and logistics, with knock-on airspace closures in Finland and the Gulf of Finland
Russian hybrid operations against NATO northern-flank states: sabotage, cyber intrusions, GNSS interference and espionage, plus arbitrary detention of Westerners inside Russia
US-led diplomacy (Witkoff-Putin channel, Oleshky ceasefire, Abu Dhabi talks) that may alter strike tempo in either direction
ind: Frequency and duration of Finnish Defence Forces air and sea restrictions off Kotka and Loviisa, and any drone debris landing on Finnish or Estonian territory
New FSB detentions of EU, UK or US nationals, or expulsions of diplomats, following each round of US-Russia talks
Confirmed attribution of sabotage or cyber attacks on Nordic-Baltic energy, telecoms or defence-industry sites, and EU visa restrictions on Russians taking effect
OUTLOOK.im: Journey management in Norway, Finland and Estonia stays routine, but itineraries through south-eastern Finland and Baltic air corridors need buffers for strike-night closures; Russia remains a no-travel destination and clients with residual staff there should maintain tested overland exit plans via the Baltics.

OUTLOOK.a: Over the next 90 days the region's risk is driven from outside it: the Iran war and Gulf shipping attacks keep Iraqi Kurdistan exposed to Iranian drone and missile strikes on exile camps near Erbil and Sulaimaniyah, with no coalition air defence since the US withdrawal, and Tehran's push to have Baghdad expel the Iranian Kurdish groups could either reduce the strike tempo or trigger a confrontation inside the Kurdistan Region. Türkiye remains physically stable for travellers but politically tightening, with the Imamoglu trial, media seizures and fund-scandal detentions feeding periodic protests in Istanbul and Ankara, and COP31 in Antalya in November bringing heavy policing and movement restrictions. Islamic State remnants in Kirkuk and Salahuddin continue low-frequency lethal attacks on security forces. The baseline is unchanged: Türkiye workable, Iraqi Kurdistan restricted, with the main upside risk being a renewed US-Israel strike on Iran.
dr: Iranian strikes on Iranian Kurdish opposition camps in Erbil and Sulaimaniyah provinces and Tehran's demand that Baghdad expel the groups
Türkiye's political crackdown (Imamoglu trial, media trustees, fund-scandal and municipal detentions) generating recurrent protests
Islamic State remnant attacks on Iraqi security forces in Kirkuk and the disputed territories after the US withdrawal
ind: Any Iranian strike causing casualties in Erbil or Sulaimaniyah cities, or near Erbil International Airport, rather than at remote camps
Formal Iraqi or KRG action to relocate or hand over Iranian Kurdish opposition members, or armed resistance to it
Police dispersal of Istanbul or Ankara demonstrations with mass detentions, or governor-imposed protest bans around the Imamoglu hearings and COP31
OUTLOOK.im: Maintain Türkiye at routine journey management with protest-day avoidance in Istanbul and Ankara and COP31 contingency planning for Antalya; keep Erbil and Sulaimaniyah on advance-approval travel with drone-strike contingency, and treat Kirkuk and the disputed territories as no-go for routine travel.

OUTLOOK.a: Over the next 90 days North Africa splits into a Critical Libya, a Tunisia whose protest cycle is widening from Tunis into the interior, and a Morocco-Algeria-Egypt core that is stable internally but increasingly exposed to external shocks. Libya's armed interference in sovereign institutions (Audit Bureau, Central Bank), repeated forced pipeline shutdowns around Zawiya and a lethal mortar accident show that oil infrastructure and Tripoli-area security remain hostage to armed-group bargaining even as the UN political track and the UNSMIL renewal proceed. Egypt's 26 October vote on defensive support for Saudi Arabia, the Houthi warnings to Cairo and the Sudan-border air strikes put Suez Canal, Red Sea and southern-frontier operations on watch, while the 31 October MINURSO vote and the US draft to wind down peacekeeping could re-ignite Polisario activity east of the berm and sharpen the Algiers-Rabat and Algiers-Paris confrontations. In Tunisia the combination of custody deaths, economic distress, the UGTT's mobilisation and continued prosecutions of opponents makes further violent flare-ups in working-class suburbs likely through the winter.
dr: Libya: armed-group pressure on oil valves, the Audit Bureau and the Central Bank in Zawiya and Tripoli, with UNSMIL's mandate renewal due 31 October
Egypt's Yemen decision (26 October vote) and Houthi retaliation threats against Suez and Red Sea assets, plus Sudan-border strikes
Tunisian unrest fuelled by deaths in custody, economic hardship and the Saied government's prosecutions of critics
ind: Reopening or prolonged closure of the Hamada-Zawiya valve, any NOC force majeure, and new armed deployments at Tripoli institutions
Outcome of Egypt's 26 October parliamentary vote and any Houthi attack or threat naming Egyptian or Suez-linked targets
Spread of Tunisian protests beyond Ettadhamen and Sfax, UGTT strike calls, and the text adopted in the 31 October MINURSO vote and Polisario's response
OUTLOOK.im: Keep Libya at no-go for routine travel with armed escort and air-evacuation planning for essential moves; add protest-day avoidance and route redundancy for Tunis and Sfax; maintain standard precautions in Morocco, Algeria and Egypt while monitoring Suez and Red Sea exposure and the Sudan and Sahel frontiers.

OUTLOOK.a: Over the next 90 days the central Sahel will remain a two-front war zone: JNIM will keep Bamako and western Mali under economic siege and continue mass-casualty assaults on isolated garrisons, while Islamic State Sahel Province, now openly at war with JNIM along the Mali-Burkina-Niger tri-border, is escalating reprisal violence against civilians in Menaka and the Tillaberi corridor. Niger's junta is simultaneously fighting ISSP in the west, bandits and traffickers on the Arlit-Agadez axis, a fuel crisis that has reached the capital, and its own army's cohesion after the August mutiny, which makes another coup attempt or a Niamey attack plausible within the horizon. In Nigeria the north-east insurgency is at its most lethal phase in years and banditry is spreading south, but Lagos, Abuja and the Niger Delta remain workable; the Abuja Ebola case is likely to stay contained if contact tracing holds, with further imported cases the main tail risk. No regional actor has the capacity to reverse these trends before the end of January.
dr: JNIM's fuel blockade of Bamako and routine overrunning of Malian and Nigerien bases, with Africa Corps unable to hold ground beyond garrison towns
ISSP-JNIM inter-jihadist war in the tri-border zone, producing reprisal massacres of civilians (Menaka, 18 Oct) and spillover into Niger's Tillaberi and the Agadez road network
State fragility in Niamey and Bamako: post-mutiny purges, fuel rationing and curfew-style measures, and a surging ISWAP/Boko Haram campaign against Nigerian army positions in Borno
ind: Any JNIM or ISSP attack inside Bamako or Niamey city limits, or a renewed mutiny or coup attempt in Niger
Casualty tolls from ISSP reprisals in Menaka/Tillaberi exceeding 50 per incident, or an attack on a mining or escorted convoy on the Arlit-Agadez or Kayes-Bamako corridors
Second confirmed Ebola case in Nigeria outside the known contact list, or further base overruns in Borno (Kukawa, Guzamala, Monguno axis)
OUTLOOK.im: Mali and Niger stay no-go for routine corporate travel for the full horizon; any essential trip needs state-level clearance, armoured movement limited to Bamako or Niamey and a pre-positioned evacuation plan given fuel rationing. Nigeria remains workable for Lagos, Abuja and Port Harcourt with advance planning, but all road movement in Borno, Zamfara, Katsina, Sokoto and the Kaduna corridor should be refused, and Abuja itineraries need medical screening contingencies and confirmed medevac cover while the Ebola response runs.

OUTLOOK.a: Somalia: As of 24 October, Laftagareen-aligned Darawish forces still hold Berdale, Dinsoor, Buurhakaba, Qansaxdheere and Awdiinle after their 15–17 October sweep through Bay region, leaving Baidoa as the only major town under the federally backed South West administration, which has announced a counteroffensive starting with Buurhakaba; the Mogadishu–Baidoa road remains cut and a fight for, or negotiated handover of, Baidoa is the base case. The electoral commission's 15 October timetable (parliament 15 April, president 15 May 2027) is rejected by the opposition, Puntland and Jubaland, sustaining the risk of armed political confrontation in Mogadishu, while in the north a UAE drone strike on 20 October in the Galgala pass and a US strike near Dhooble on 17 October precede an expected new Puntland offensive against al-Shabaab. IOM projects up to 874,000 flood displacements by December with the Shabelle above its high flood-risk level at Jowhar; no large or complex al-Shabaab attack in Mogadishu or at Aden Adde airport was wire-reported between 10 and 24 October, and rating 4, rising trend and no-go posture outside the airport/Halane enclave are retained. The Horn is carrying two wars and a widening set of secondary fronts into the 90-day horizon. Sudan's conflict has become a long-range drone war in which the UN counted at least 306 drone deaths in the first three weeks of October, and the 19 October Amiet market strike shows that RSF supply corridors through Abyei and South Sudan are now targets, dragging Juba into the conflict as its own election timetable and Machar trial keep the transition brittle. In Ethiopia, federal control of Tigray's towns has reduced fighting there but hardened the standoff with Eritrea, where Abiy's 19 October warning and Rubio's description of troop surges on both sides of the border keep a state-on-state war plausible within weeks, while the lethal Moyale fighting between Oromia and Somali regional forces opened a new front on the Kenyan border. Kenya and Djibouti remain the workable hubs, but Kenya's Ebola cluster, al-Shabaab activity along the Somali border and a fatal construction-safety record in Nairobi add friction, and Djibouti's exposure rises with every escalation in Yemen's Red Sea war.
dr: Drone proliferation on both sides of Sudan's war, with strikes on markets, transport hubs, dams and airports far behind the front and spillover into Abyei and South Sudan
Ethiopia-Eritrea confrontation frozen at the border after federal recapture of Tigray's towns, with severed ties, mutual UN complaints and Abiy's sea-access ambitions as the escalation logic

Ethnic-regional and intercommunal violence along the Ethiopia-Kenya and Kenya-Somalia borders (Moyale, Mandera) layered on Kenya's Ebola cluster and cost-of-living pressures ahead of the 2027 election
ind: Further Sudanese strikes on South Sudanese or Abyei territory, or any South Sudanese military response, after the UN Security Council's 23 October statement
Cross-border artillery, drone or ground action at Zalambessa, Rama or Assab, or a formal Ethiopian ultimatum to Asmara following the 19 October warning
Ebola cases in Kenya outside the quarantined cluster, or Moyale fighting crossing into Kenyan territory with Kenyan security-force casualties
OUTLOOK.im: Treat Sudan, South Sudan outside Juba and northern Ethiopia as no-go and Eritrea as avoid; plan Addis Ababa, Nairobi and Djibouti itineraries with advance security and health screening, keep contingency routes out of Addis that do not depend on the northern corridor, and build Ebola-related medical and evacuation caveats into every Kenya journey plan over the next 90 days.

OUTLOOK.a: Over the next 90 days the DRC conflict is more likely to widen than to settle: Kabila's FRN gives the Rwanda-backed M23 rebellion a national political project aimed at Kinshasa, and the government's response (party bans, arrests, a defence council on a war footing) narrows the space for the Doha and Washington tracks, where the 3 October economic-framework signing was already cancelled. Fighting is expected to persist in the South Kivu highlands and midlands (Walungu, Kaziba, Minembwe, toward Uvira) and in Masisi/Walikale, with ADF and CODECO killings continuing in Ituri and Beni. The Bundibugyo Ebola outbreak, near 10,000 cases and spreading to new provinces and to Kenya and Nigeria, will keep adding health, access and border-screening friction through year-end. Kinshasa and the Katangan copper belt should stay operable but with higher political-policing risk, as the Kolwezi detentions of Chinese miners show.
dr: FRN/M23 attempt to translate Kabila's leadership into territorial or political gains, and Kinshasa's counter-mobilisation of FARDC, Wazalendo and foreign contractors
Collapse or survival of the US-brokered Washington Accords and Qatar-mediated Doha track, including any new US sanctions on Rwandan officials
Trajectory of the Ebola outbreak (case growth in North Kivu/Ituri, new provinces, imported cases abroad) and the insecurity constraining the response
ind: FRN/M23 advance beyond current lines toward Uvira town, Walungu or Walikale, or a declared offensive toward Kisangani/Katanga
Mass arrests or violence against banned-party supporters in Kinshasa or Lubumbashi; restrictions on Kabila-linked media
Weekly Ebola case counts rising above the 500-plus-per-week level recorded in mid-October, or confirmation of a ninth province or sustained transmission in Kenya or Nigeria
OUTLOOK.im: Maintain no-go status for the Kivus and Ituri and treat Kinshasa, Lubumbashi and Kolwezi as elevated-risk with pre-cleared itineraries, Ebola health-screening contingencies and legal/consular support plans for expatriate staff exposed to immigration and mining-enforcement sweeps.

OUTLOOK.a: The next 90 days hinge on Brazil's 25 October runoff, which polls put at a 50-50 tie with mutual disqualification petitions pending at the electoral court: a narrow or contested result would bring protests to Brasília, São Paulo and Rio and judicial uncertainty into November, but Brazil's institutions have absorbed contested votes before and the risk to corporate travellers is disruption rather than violence. Colombia is the region's deteriorating theatre: President de la Espriella's bombing campaign against the ELN and FARC dissidents (five strikes since August, nine killed in Cauca on 22 October) is drawing drone and car-bomb retaliation against police stations and highway infrastructure in Cauca, Cesar and Catatumbo, and that cycle will intensify rather than ease through year-end. Venezuela is in a slow, US-managed transition in which the opposition has reactivated the street while talks with the interim government produce incremental guarantees but no election date; the baseline is stable for low-profile business travel to Caracas, with a tail risk of a crackdown or a US policy shift.
dr: Brazil's runoff outcome and whether the losing camp accepts it or pursues court and street challenges
Colombia's air-strike-and-retaliation cycle between the de la Espriella government and the ELN/FARC dissidents, now reaching fixed police posts in Cesar and the Pan-American Highway
Pace of Venezuela's US-backed talks versus the opposition's street mobilisation and Machado's attempted return
ind: Margin and acceptance of Brazil's 25 October result; any electoral-court ruling on the disqualification petitions; crowd sizes in Brasília and São Paulo on 25-27 October
ELN or dissident attacks on urban targets, toll plazas or oil infrastructure in Colombia within two weeks of each new bombing; casualty counts among police and soldiers
A fixed Venezuelan election date, detentions after opposition marches, and whether Machado is allowed to re-enter the country
OUTLOOK.im: Plan Brazil movements around 25-27 October with contingency for closures in capital-city centres and a contested count; hold Colombia at advance-approval status with no road movement in Cauca, Cesar, Catatumbo or Arauca; keep Venezuela programmes low-profile with standing distance from all marches in central Caracas.

AAIA.s: On a Sunday afternoon a suicide car bomb was driven into the gate of the Elite Hotel on Lido Beach, a popular weekend venue for Mogadishu's politicians and business community, and a small team of gunmen then stormed the building. Security forces fought room to room for roughly seven hours before the last attacker was killed. The UN later put the toll at at least 17 dead. The attack re-established the Al-Shabaab 'gate VBIED then assault team' template against soft, high-status venues that would recur through 2024.

AAIA.tg: Hotel near AAIA used by officials and officers
AAIA.s: A car bomb detonated at the entrance of Hotel Afrik, on the main road between the city and the airport, and four gunmen fought their way inside. The siege lasted several hours; among the dead was a retired Somali general. Civilians trapped in the hotel were rescued by security forces, and the UN Special Representative condemned the attack the next day. The venue's location — on the airport approach and within sight of the Halane access route — made it the closest hotel-siege to AAIA in the period.

AAIA.tg: Civilians and soldiers at a checkpoint
AAIA.s: A suicide bomber wearing an explosive vest walked into a corrugated-tin teashop beside a government security checkpoint in Wadajir, the district that physically borders both the airport and the AU mission headquarters, and detonated among off-duty soldiers and civilians. At least 11 people were killed. Al-Shabaab claimed the attack; the prime minister condemned it as a 'barbaric act'. It illustrates the group's use of low-cost person-borne devices against checkpoint clusters on the airport's landward side.

AAIA.tg: AU convoy (claimed); school and civilians hit
AAIA.s: At 07:30 a suicide bomber in an SUV detonated beside a passing convoy on a busy Hodan road just as pupils were arriving at the neighbouring Mocaasir Primary and Secondary School. Al-Shabaab said the target was an AU Mission convoy; the blast instead killed eight people and injured 17, including teachers and children, and heavily damaged the school. The incident is a reminder that convoy-targeted VBIEDs on the KM4–airport axis produce heavy collateral casualties in the dense districts between the city centre and AAIA.

A suicide car bomber rammed a convoy on the main road leading to the AAIA/Halane entrance, killing around eight people. Al-Shabaab claimed the attack and said it targeted a convoy carrying Western contractors and security staff. The strike demonstrated the vulnerability of the single approach road that all airport and Halane traffic must use, and prompted a tightening of convoy procedures for the compound.

Gunmen penetrated the eastern area of Aden Adde International Airport and attacked a military position inside the perimeter; black smoke was visible near the runway during the firefight. Five people, including an AMISOM soldier, were killed before the two attackers were shot. The assault was coordinated with twin suicide bombings in Beledweyne the same day that killed dozens, including a federal MP. It remains the only confirmed ground penetration of the AAIA perimeter in the period and exposed gaps on the airfield's eastern (beach-side) edge.

AAIA.tg: Hotel used by officials and businessmen
AAIA.s: Two car bombs breached the Hayat Hotel's defences on a Friday evening and a team of gunmen barricaded themselves inside with hostages. Security forces took around 30 hours to clear the building floor by floor; 21 people were killed and over 100 injured, many by the second blast that hit responders and bystanders. It was the first major Mogadishu attack after President Hassan Sheikh Mohamud's 2022 election and triggered his declaration of 'total war' on Al-Shabaab.
AAIA.src: Widely reported; 30-hour siege referenced at thedefensepost.com/2025/04/06

AAIA.s: At around 14:00 a vehicle bomb exploded at the Zobe junction outside the Ministry of Education; minutes later a second VBIED detonated as ambulances and crowds converged, destroying at least one ambulance. More than 120 people were killed and over 300 injured — the deadliest attack in Somalia since the October 2017 truck bomb at the same junction. Al-Shabaab admitted responsibility on 1 November, framing the ministry as a legitimate target. The sequenced 'second blast on first responders' tactic is the defining feature of this event.

AAIA.loc: Villa Rose Hotel, Bondhere (near Villa Somalia)
AAIA.tg: Hotel frequented by ministers and MPs
AAIA.s: Gunmen stormed the Villa Rose Hotel, a short walk from the presidential palace and a known residence for ministers, after a car bomb at the gate. The siege lasted roughly 20 hours; around nine people were killed and the environment minister was among the wounded. The attack showed Al-Shabaab's willingness to strike inside the government district despite the heightened security that followed the October Zobe bombing.

A bomb exploded in the Pearl Beach hotel restaurant on a Friday evening and seven gunmen then entered the building, taking diners hostage. Security forces freed 84 people during an overnight operation and killed all seven attackers; six civilians and three soldiers died. The attack repeated the 2020 Elite Hotel pattern on the same stretch of Lido Beach, underlining that beachfront leisure venues 4–5 km from AAIA remain a preferred soft target.

Several mortar rounds were fired into the airport complex, one of which killed a Ugandan soldier of the UN Guard Unit. It was the first lethal indirect-fire attack on AAIA in the 2024–25 series and marked a shift from ground assaults to stand-off IDF against the airport and Halane.

An attacker in military uniform opened fire on a group of Emirati and Bahraini trainers at the General Gordon base, killing four UAE soldiers and a Bahraini officer. Al-Shabaab claimed the attack. The incident highlighted the insider-threat risk at training sites and led to a review of vetting for foreign-supported units.

A suicide bomber blew himself up at the gate of the SYL Hotel, adjacent to the presidential palace, and five or six gunmen stormed inside. The siege ran for about 13 hours; three guards, two security officers and three soldiers were killed along with all the attackers, and 27 people were injured. The hotel had been attacked twice before, and the operation showed that even the palace perimeter zone could be penetrated by a small assault team.

Al-Shabaab detainees in Mogadishu Central Prison seized weapons, threw grenades and attempted a mass breakout. Custodial Corps and army reinforcements contained the attempt after a gunfight that left five prisoners and three soldiers dead and 21 injured. The government said no one escaped; Al-Shabaab claimed hundreds freed. The incident pointed to weapons and communications reaching detainees inside the capital's main prison.

A suicide car bomb exploded outside a café near the Daljirka Daahsoon monument where crowds had gathered to watch the Euro 2024 final. Reports of the toll range from five to more than nine killed, with about 20 injured. The attack, a day after the prison breakout attempt, targeted a predictable civilian gathering and showed the group's attention to timing against televised events.

On a Friday evening a suicide bomber detonated at the Beach View hotel and gunmen then opened fire on beach-goers and diners along Lido Beach. Thirty-seven civilians and a soldier were killed before the six attackers were shot — the deadliest attack in the capital in 2024 and the third major assault on the Lido strip since 2020. Lido's open beachfront and crowd density make it the hardest soft target in the city to protect.

An IED concealed inside a crowded tea shop in Daynile detonated mid-afternoon, killing at least 20 people, several of them security personnel who frequented the venue. The attack came two weeks after Lido Beach and showed Al-Shabaab's reach into the north-western districts along the Afgooye corridor — the same Daynile checkpoints that produce the bulk of Mogadishu's grenade and IED events in 2026.

A suicide car bomber attacked a NISA checkpoint on the Afgooye highway, the main western entry to the city, killing ten people including seven intelligence officers. Al-Shabaab claimed responsibility. The Afgooye corridor is the primary route by which VBIEDs are assembled in Lower Shabelle and moved toward the capital, and checkpoints on it are repeatedly targeted.

Six mortar rounds landed across the airport and the Halane compound, injuring several people and damaging residences used by ATMIS personnel and diplomats. No group claimed it. It was the second barrage of 2024 and showed the attackers' ability to range both the airfield and the diplomatic enclave from firing points in the city's southern districts.

Mortar rounds struck inside Halane, killing three people and injuring several; ATMIS condemned it as a 'deadly mortar attack'. This was the most lethal of the 2024 barrages and prompted additional counter-IDF measures around the compound's southern and western approaches.

AAIA.loc: Ceelgaabta, presidential motorcade route to airport
AAIA.s: A roadside bomb detonated beside the presidential motorcade at Ceelgaabta as it travelled from Villa Somalia toward the airport. The president was unhurt but reports put the dead at between four and a dozen, including a journalist. Al-Shabaab claimed the attack, which coincided with its spring offensive in Middle and Lower Shabelle and the loss of several towns to the group. It was the closest Al-Shabaab has come to the head of state in the period.

A day after the motorcade bombing, mortar rounds hit the area of the airport where UN personnel board aircraft and landed inside Halane near the Movcon area, just as Ethiopian Prime Minister Abiy Ahmed was arriving. Airport sirens sounded and flights were held; no casualties were reported. The timing against a VIP arrival is the clearest example of Al-Shabaab using IDF for political signalling rather than casualties.

AAIA.loc: AAIA open area, Halane, Kaawo Godey
AAIA.s: Around 06:05 six mortar rounds fell on open ground inside the airport, on Halane and on the Kaawo Godey residential area outside the fence, injuring a woman and a young man. A Turkish Airlines flight diverted to Djibouti and EgyptAir cancelled its service for the day. AUSSOM reported no casualties among its troops. The barrage followed a mortar attack on Warta Nabada and Boondheere the previous day, part of a sustained spring IDF campaign.

At least five mortar shells landed inside the Halane perimeter early on a Monday morning; it was not immediately clear whether anyone was hurt or which installations were hit. It was the third strike on the compound in roughly six weeks and reinforced the assessment that Al-Shabaab could fire on Halane at will from the southern districts.

A bomber dressed in military uniform joined a queue of young recruits at the Damaanyo base gate and detonated a vest at about 09:20, killing 15 recruits and five civilians and injuring 15. Al-Shabaab claimed the attack with inflated casualty figures. The event showed the continued ability to place a person-borne device at a predictable, crowded military access point in Hodan, roughly 3.5 km from AAIA.

At least six mortar rounds hit Halane and properties near the airport two days after the Damaanyo bombing; emergency sirens sounded along the airport perimeter and Al-Shabaab claimed the attack within hours. Somali Guardian counted it as the fourth attack on the base in recent weeks. Damage was limited to property, but the cadence (four barrages in nine weeks) is the densest IDF campaign against AAIA/Halane in the period.

A suicide bomber reached the morning roll-call at the Jaalle Siyaad academy, headquarters of the 14th October Brigade, and detonated among officers; gunfire followed. Four SNA officers were killed and several injured. Six senior officers were detained over the security breach and the ministry restricted reporting. Coming two years after a deadlier 2023 bombing at the same academy, it underlined persistent insider and access-control weaknesses at Hodan military sites.

AAIA.loc: Godka Jilow prison, near Villa Somalia
AAIA.t: VBIED + armed assault in NISA-style vehicles/uniforms
AAIA.s: A car bomb breached the entrance of the Godka Jilow underground prison near the presidential palace and a seven-man team in military-style uniforms, driving vehicles painted to resemble NISA's, attempted to free detained fighters. The siege lasted about six hours before all seven attackers were killed; the government said no prisoners escaped and did not publish its own losses. The attack came hours after the city reopened dozens of roads and is the most recent confirmed complex assault by Al-Shabaab in the capital.

AAIA.t: Political violence: government shelling/assault on opposition compounds
AAIA.tg: Residences of ex-PM Khaire and ex-President Sharif
AAIA.s: Over two days government forces shelled and assaulted the Barmuudo compound of former PM Hassan Ali Khaire and then the Marinayo residence of former President Sharif Sheikh Ahmed, after the collapse of election talks and the expiry of the presidential mandate. NISA chief Mahad Salad negotiated Khaire's withdrawal and escorted him back to his residence inside the AAIA perimeter, where opposition leaders had been based before dispersing to clan areas. Western ambassadors, speaking from Halane, pressed for a halt. Casualty figures were never verified. Not an Al-Shabaab event, but the clearest case of Mogadishu's political conflict reaching the airport perimeter.

Defence Minister Ahmed Moalim Fiqi said authorities had removed 260 armed men from opposition leaders' residences in Mogadishu, alleging the UAE had armed the opposition and that Puntland- and Jubaland-linked forces had been brought into the city. He denied any plan to arrest opposition leaders. Only the government's account is available. The operation is the precursor indicator for a repeat of the June clashes.

AAIA.loc: Hormuud HQ, Bakara Market & airport road
AAIA.s: Police entered Hormuud's headquarters in Bakara Market and its main management office on the road to the airport under a court warrant, reportedly in connection with the Southwest State fighting. No violence was reported. The relevance for AAIA is the use of the airport road for a politically charged security operation and the risk of escalation involving Somalia's largest private company.
