BRIEF.CZ: No terrorism, sabotage, violent unrest or major transport disruption was confirmed in Czechia between 10 and 24 October. The risk remains political: after losing the 17 October Senate runoffs, the Babiš coalition on 23 October fast-tracked a bill moving Czech Television and Czech Radio onto the state budget with a roughly 15% funding cut, extending the debate into Saturday 24 October over opposition obstruction, a move critics call a power grab; public-media staff have announced strike action. Czechia sits inside the regional Russian hybrid-threat pattern (Germany's 21 October threat upgrade, Austria's 23 October expulsion of four Russian diplomats), but nothing in the window points to an active plot on Czech soil and business travel to Prague is routine.
BRIEF.GB: The UK picture through 24 October remains dominated by state threats rather than street disorder: the two men re-arrested on 20 October under the National Security Act for assisting Iranian intelligence in the RAF Fairford investigation can be held until 27 October, MI5 said on 13 October that Iran and Russia are both expanding hybrid campaigns, and the Home Secretary set out new sanctions and powers on 12 October. The national terrorism threat level remains Severe. No attack occurred between 10 and 24 October and daily business travel is unaffected, but US-linked military sites, Jewish community venues and Iranian-dissident targets carry elevated risk; the violent cost-of-living unrest in France, Italy, Belgium and Spain has not spread to Britain.
BRIEF.DE: Germany's state-threat environment hardened in the final week of the window: federal prosecutors arrested a Ukrainian national in Brandenburg on 22 October for gathering military intelligence for Russia, including on NATO eastern-flank sites and defence-industry production, one day after the Bundeswehr rated the Russian sabotage threat to its own forces as significant for the first time, and Chancellor Merz said on 22 October that Germany is the target of intensive espionage and more such cases will follow. A perimeter breach at Leipzig/Halle airport on 17-18 October closed the north runway before two learner drivers admitted crashing through the fence. Nothing new was confirmed on 23-24 October; for travellers the practical impact remains sporadic airport disruption and heightened security around military, Jewish and Israeli sites, and the violent unrest in France and Italy has not spread to Germany.
BRIEF.SK: No terrorism, sabotage, violent protest or transport disruption was confirmed in Slovakia between 10 and 24 October. The risk remains political: the Fico government holds the first Slovak-Russian intergovernmental commission since 2022 in Moscow on Monday 26 October, focused on gas, oil and nuclear energy, and has restored military attachés with Russia for the first time in four years, deepening divergence from EU and NATO allies, a week in which Austria expelled four Russian diplomats for espionage. Business travel to Bratislava and Košice is routine.
BRIEF.AT: Austria's window closed with a counter-intelligence move rather than a security incident: on 23 October the foreign ministry declared four Vienna-based Russian diplomats, three at the embassy and one at the OSCE delegation, personae non gratae for activities incompatible with their status, and Moscow said it would respond. Earlier, two Ukrainians arrested on 5 October remain held on suspicion of spying while two journalists detained on 8 October were released without charge. A university-funding demonstration of tens of thousands in Vienna on 22 October passed peacefully, and the violent cost-of-living unrest seen in France, Italy, Belgium and Spain has not reached Austria; the threat to travellers is low.
BRIEF.BE: Belgium remains the most exposed of the smaller core states to the French contagion: union strike days on 9 and 12 October disrupted Brussels Airport, rail, public transport and schools, and student-led protests turned violent in Brussels and Liège on 17 October, with police using tear gas and water cannon. The core cabinet again ended 2027 budget talks without agreement late on 21 October and Prime Minister De Wever told parliament on 22 October a deal is now expected next week, so the trigger for further union action stays live and the socialist FGTB holds a mandate for a general strike in late November if its red lines are crossed. No new violence was confirmed on 22-24 October; expect Friday and weekend disruption in central Brussels and plan airport transfers with margin while the budget is unresolved.
BRIEF.IT: Italy enters Saturday 24 October with security forces deploying massively for cost-of-living protests planned in eight cities including Rome and Milan, where 500 soldiers patrol under the 20 October decree that also created a violent-protest offence after the 17-18 October riots in Milan, Turin, Bologna, Brescia and Bergamo. The southern trucker roadblocks over diesel prices, which emptied supermarket shelves and fuel pumps, halted buffalo mozzarella production, left Crotone and Reggio Calabria airports without aviation fuel and hampered Naples ambulances, began lifting on 22 October after the cabinet approved an aid decree, with Calabria and Sicily suspending and Campania expected to follow. Avoid city centres in Milan, Rome, Turin, Bologna, Florence and Genoa on 24 October and keep fuel, routing and regional-airport contingencies for southern Italy until roadblocks are confirmed cleared.
BRIEF.ES: Spain's picture shifted from weather to politics in the final days of the window: Storm Adam's floods in the Valencia region and Catalonia on 17-19 October killed four, with clean-up in Oliva, Pego and the Marina Alta still disrupting secondary roads, but on 21 October the first pre-campaign rally by Vox leader Santiago Abascal in A Coruña drew about 5,000 counter-protesters and ended in police charges, rubber bullets, burning bins, around a dozen injured and arrests, with a second night of clashes on 22 October, the first violent spill-over of the European unrest wave into Spain. With the 29 November early election, a 24-hour Renfe drivers' strike on 29 October and a union general strike on 11 November ahead, expect further confrontations around far-right rallies and housing protests; the 18 October Basque terrorism arrests appear contained and crime indicators are unchanged.
BRIEF.FR: France's risk rose on the eve of the 24 October protest day: a gunman firing an automatic weapon from a car killed one person and seriously wounded four, including a 12-year-old, at three locations in Trappes and La Verrière west of Paris on the morning of 23 October before his arrest in Coignières, and the national anti-terrorism prosecutor opened a murder-in-connection-with-terrorism inquiry with a racial aggravating circumstance, which Macron called a racist terrorist attack. The same day Interior Minister Nuñez announced 70,000 security personnel, 20% more than on 17 October, for Saturday's cost-of-living protests, with all demonstrations banned in Lyon, Nice and Montpellier, curfews extended to adults in Marseille, Paris marches confined to Bastille-Nation, the Louvre, Orsay and Picasso museums closed and student groups vowing to keep mobilising after meeting Macron; courts have jailed 217 people over the 17 October riots, which saw some 2,700 arrests. Storm Adam also killed four in Bouches-du-Rhône and Haute-Corse on 20-21 October. Avoid central Paris, Lyon, Marseille, Montpellier and Orléans (National Rally congress) on 24-25 October and plan movements around curfew and protest-ban perimeters; risk stays high for at least two to three weeks.
BRIEF.PL: Poland's window was front-loaded: three school stabbings in four days that killed a custodian and triggered checks of nearly 50,000 schools, German arrests announced on 12 October of two Turkish nationals suspected of the Russian-directed Starlink station arson near Warsaw, and the 16 October detention in Łódź, announced 19 October, of a Polish-Ukrainian reservist on an officer course on spying suspicion. Nothing new was confirmed between 20 and 24 October, but Tusk's 17 October warning of larger-scale Russian sabotage and provocations before Christmas, with railways and border crossings supplying Ukraine most exposed, is reinforced by Germany's 21 October threat upgrade, its 22 October spy arrest and Austria's 23 October expulsion of four Russian diplomats. Warsaw remains fully workable.
BRIEF.NO: Norway remains a low-risk operating environment: the only in-window events affecting movement were the heavily policed 20 October Oslo talks between Zelensky, Witkoff, Støre and Stubb and Zelensky's 21 October Storting visit, both of which passed without incident, and the one domestic security operation was Økokrim's 14 October arrest of five people in the Bergen area over fraud and bribery on NATO ship-supply contracts. No violence, sabotage or transport disruption affecting travellers was reported between 10 and 24 October, and nothing new emerged on 22-24 October beyond routine economic and political news. Friction with Russia over the Arctic, sanctions alignment and espionage continues without any change to travel advice.
BRIEF.FI: Finland is safe for travel and operations, but the south-eastern coast between Loviisa and the Russian border is subject to short-notice air and sea closures whenever Ukraine mounts large strikes on St Petersburg; the Defence Forces imposed such restrictions on three consecutive mornings on 16, 17 and 18 October with no drones crossing into Finland, and no new restrictions were reported on 22-24 October. On 21 October the state IT centre Valtori took the government's public web services offline as a precaution against two critical PHP vulnerabilities, a disruption to e-services rather than a breach. No violence occurred on Finnish territory between 10 and 24 October; the eastern land border remains closed to civilian traffic and GNSS interference persists in the Gulf of Finland.
BRIEF.EE: No significant security incident occurred on Estonian territory between 10 and 24 October 2026; in-window reporting is dominated by deterrence and resilience measures, including Foreign Minister Tsahkna's 15 October warning that Russia will intensify hybrid attacks and the nearly 32 million euros in EU funding confirmed on 16 October for eastern-border drone surveillance. On 23 October the Prosecutor's Office closed its investigation into the stray drone that hit the Auvere power plant chimney on 25 March, finding no deliberate activity aimed at Estonia but unable to establish the drone's origin. Travel to Tallinn is routine; vehicle traffic through the Narva crossing remains suspended and any onward travel into Russia carries serious detention risk.
BRIEF.RU: Russia's two principal cities remain under sustained Ukrainian drone attack: after the 18 October assault that killed one and injured 15 in St Petersburg and set the oil terminal ablaze, 630 drones were sent towards Moscow overnight on 21-22 October wounding two, and on 23 October a daytime raid forced Rosaviatsia to halt flights at all four Moscow airports and Sheremetyevo to move passengers into shelters, with Mayor Sobyanin reporting 155 drones towards the region overnight and more than 20 downed on approach to the city during the afternoon. Air travel is unreliable and Western nationals face arbitrary detention on espionage or sabotage pretexts, with the FSB announcing the arrest of a German, a Swede and a Japanese journalist in the past fortnight; the 21 October release of American Stephen Hubbard during Witkoff's talks with Putin, and the 23 October Oleshky ceasefire agreement with trilateral talks planned in Abu Dhabi in early November, show detainees and local truces are being traded as diplomatic currency without any easing of the strike campaign. Treat Russia as no-go for travel; remaining staff need independent exit plans via Finland or the Baltics, noting Finland's land border is closed to civilian crossing.
BRIEF.TR: No terrorist attack or mass-casualty security incident was recorded in Türkiye between 10 and 24 October; the operational picture is dominated by the aftermath of the 14 October Istanbul flood disaster (eight dead per AFP on 19 October) and by the political crackdown, with the Halk TV seizure on 14 October, continuing detentions of opposition-run municipal officials, and Reuters-reported detention orders for 31 suspects in the investment-fund probe on 21 October. Istanbul hosted Canada's prime minister on 22-23 October and a seven-nation foreign ministers' meeting on 23 October without incident, but press organisations called nationwide anti-censorship demonstrations for 24 October in Istanbul, Ankara, Izmir and other cities, and the Imamoglu trial calendar plus November's COP31 in Antalya keep the likelihood of protests and heavy policing elevated.
BRIEF.IQ: The Kurdistan Region remains the most active theatre: a missile was fired at an Iranian Kurdish opposition camp north-east of Erbil on 21 October (Reuters), the latest in a series of Iranian strikes on exile camps on 8, 12 and 17 October, and Tehran's ambassador said on 20 October that Baghdad had agreed to expel or hand over the opposition groups (AFP), a claim absent from the Iraqi statement and rejected by the groups themselves. Elsewhere, a roadside bomb killed an army brigadier and a soldier south of Kirkuk on 14 October, a tanker was struck by an unknown projectile 30 nautical miles south-east of Al Faw on 20 October (UKMTO), and Iraq closed the Sheeb crossing with Iran on 21 October for a security review. No new strike or lethal attack was reported between 22 and 24 October, but with coalition air defences gone since the 30 September US withdrawal, Erbil province remains exposed to further unanswered Iranian strikes while commercial flights to Erbil and Sulaimaniyah continue.
BRIEF.MA: Morocco recorded no kinetic security incident between 10 and 24 October that a wire service confirmed; the environment remains political and workable nationwide outside the Western Sahara berm zone. The El Mansouri coalition government, sworn in on 16 October, presented its 2027-2031 programme to parliament on 19 October (Reuters), while the Ceuta migration dispute with Spain (Reuters, 19 October) and Algeria's 11 October announcement of 61 Moroccans arrested in Oran keep regional tensions elevated ahead of the 31 October Security Council vote on MINURSO, for which a US zero draft proposing to end the peacekeeping mandate in April 2027 began circulating on 22 October according to RFI and regional media, drawing a Polisario threat to quit the process. Small sectoral protests (preschool teachers, working students) outside parliament in Rabat on 19-22 October were dispersed without wire-reported casualties; the last notable kinetic incident remains the Polisario rocket attack near Smara on 5 May 2026 (older).
BRIEF.DZ: No terrorist attack, clash or significant protest was wire-confirmed in Algeria between 10 and 24 October; the environment is stable but heavily securitised and the state continues to frame domestic problems as foreign-backed subversion. The DGSN's 11 October announcement that 61 Moroccan nationals were arrested in Oran on suspicion of preparing sabotage (Le Monde/AFP) keeps the temperature high with Rabat ahead of the 31 October MINURSO vote, and Reuters reported on 23 October that Algiers has ordered urea producers to halt exports to France on top of an unofficial near-blanket ban on French imports since July, confirming a combative external posture that also saw the Madrid summit postponed and ties with the UAE ruptured in September. The jihadist threat is low but not zero (failed suicide attack near a Blida police station in April and army-militant clashes in Tebessa in March, both older); the Sahel border belt and the far south remain off-limits for routine corporate travel, and French-linked businesses should expect continued administrative friction.
BRIEF.TN: Tunisia's risk profile is rising: on 22 October police fired tear gas at protesters in Ettadhamen, a suburb of Tunis, after the death of a man in custody, with parallel clashes in Jebeniana and Agareb in Sfax governorate and student protests in Sfax city (Reuters), and AFP reported on 23 October that protesters in Ettadhamen burned tyres and blocked roads overnight with no confirmed casualties or arrests, five days after the UGTT-led march of 17 October, the largest show of opposition to President Saied in years. On 21 October a military court sentenced opposition leader Olfa Hamdi, a US citizen, to four years in prison for plotting against state security (Reuters/AFP), the latest in a series of prosecutions of critics. Reuters reported fears of a wider wave of violent protest over living conditions and public services; expect further protest calls, possible strike action and localised unrest in working-class suburbs and the interior through the coming weeks, while the Chaambi and Libyan-frontier zones remain restricted.
BRIEF.EG: No terrorist attack, Sinai incident or domestic unrest was wire-confirmed in Egypt between 10 and 24 October, but the external-security profile is rising. Parliament votes on 26 October on President Sisi's request to authorise military support for Saudi Arabia against the Houthis; Sisi said on 21 October that any support would be limited to defending Saudi territory and would not include an attack on Yemen, and on 22 October Foreign Minister Abdelatty urged exploring 'every opportunity' for a political settlement after delivering Sisi's letter to the Saudi crown prince (Reuters). The Houthi-run parliament has warned Cairo that intervention would threaten its internal stability, so a deployment would expose Egyptian and Suez-linked targets to retaliation; on the southern frontier, the 10 October air strikes on the Jabal al-Uqaydat gold-mining site killed at least 72 miners according to Sudan's Emergency Lawyers (AFP/France 24; AP initially reported at least 13 dead), with Egypt silent on the attack. North Sinai remains a restricted military zone and the Sudan border belt should be treated as no-go, while Cairo, Alexandria, the Canal cities and Red Sea resorts remain workable with standard precautions.
BRIEF.LY: Libya remains Critical and the trend is rising: on 22 October individuals entered the AGOCO crude receiving station near the Zawiya refinery and shut the valve on the Hamada-Zawiya pipeline, cutting output at the Hamada and Tahara fields (Reuters) in the second forced pipeline closure in western Libya in five weeks, with no wire-confirmed reopening as of 24 October; on 21 October armed men stormed the National Audit Bureau in Tripoli to impose a disputed deputy head, drawing UNSMIL's strongest condemnation and a warning of targeted sanctions; and on 18 October an 82mm mortar blast killed at least nine Anti-Threat Security Agency personnel during training in Zawiya (Reuters). Institutional fragmentation deepened on 22 October when the east-based House of Representatives accepted in principle the resignation of Central Bank governor Naji Issa and backed board member Fowzi Abukhzam as interim governor while the High Council of State split over the move and the bank condemned a forced entry into its Tripoli headquarters (Reuters, 23 October), raising the risk of a renewed contest over the central bank. The political track is comparatively convergent (SRSG Tetteh told the Security Council on 14 October the process had made 'encouraging progress'; the HoR's 20 October approval of the 2019 Türkiye maritime deal drew rejections from Greece, Egypt, Israel and the EU) and UNSMIL's mandate renewal is due by 31 October; the August drone strikes on the Zawiya refinery, the September Sharara-Zawiya shutdown and the 10 August car-bomb killing of the LNA intelligence chief in Benghazi remain the baseline of targeted violence and infrastructure disruption.
BRIEF.NG: Between 10 and 24 October the north-east recorded its heaviest military losses in years: ISWAP/Boko Haram overran the Guzamala-Mairari base on 13-14 October (Reuters: at least 10 soldiers, five civilians and a forest guard; AFP sources: 15 soldiers and five CJTF) and a mine-and-ambush on a patrol near Gamboru Ngala on 17 October killed 10 soldiers and five CJTF (Reuters, 19 Oct), while in the north-west bandits killed at least 20 in a military-escorted traders' convoy in Bukkuyum, Zamfara, on 10 October (Reuters, 12 Oct), so armed escort is not sufficient mitigation on rural roads. The imported Bundibugyo Ebola case in Abuja remains the only confirmed case: on 23 October the health minister said genomic analysis links it to the Kenyan index case and that contacts are quarantined with some tests negative and others pending (Reuters), the NCDC begins daily public updates from 24 October, and the Swiss government told Reuters the patient did not travel to Congo; travellers should expect airport screening, avoid non-essential use of private clinics in the FCT and confirm medevac cover. Lagos and the south had no wire-confirmed major incident in the window; rating held at 3, trend rising.
BRIEF.NE: The deadliest incident between 10 and 24 October hit the north rather than the jihadist-hit west: gunmen in three vehicles ambushed two escorted passenger buses on the Arlit-Agadez road on 20 October, killing at least 11 (AFP; the Agadez governor later put the toll at 12 including a soldier), on the only corridor used by mining and humanitarian traffic to the uranium belt, and the military escort aboard did not prevent it. The release on 21 October of Austrian Eva Gretzmacher, 76, and Swiss Claudia Abbt, 69, both kidnapped in Agadez in 2025 (BBC/DW, 22 Oct), closes two long hostage cases but confirms foreigners in Agadez are kidnap targets. The civil picture keeps deteriorating: with a fuel-export ban in force since 12 October and shortages reaching Niamey on 18 October (AFP), the government has banned public fuel sales from 21:00 to 06:00 from 19 October (ANP), making night movement and journey timing unreliable, while frontline frustration after the late-September ISSP assaults in Tillaberi and the junta's purge of critics since the failed 29 August mutiny keep coup and reprisal risk elevated; rating held at 4.
BRIEF.ML: Mali remains in open, multi-front war as of 24 October: JNIM has held the Bamako approaches under a fuel blockade since late April, with fuel reaching the capital only in large escorted tanker convoys, while Islamic State Sahel Province's killing of at least 48 civilians (AFP sources: 40 to more than 50; Reuters sources: up to 70+) in Daoussahak camps around Tinabow and Tagadayat in Menaka on 18-19 October, described by Reuters' sources as reprisal for killings of suspected informants by the MSA militia and Africa Corps, marks an escalation in the east even as ISSP and JNIM fight each other across the Burkina border; the army said on 19 October it struck a major ISSP base 65 km south-west of Menaka (AP). The army's re-entry into Kidal on 6 October is a morale win but changes nothing on supply. Human Rights Watch's 19 October report (Reuters, Al Jazeera) documents indiscriminate Malian and Africa Corps drone strikes and the execution of 19 captured soldiers by JNIM and FLA fighters, and HRW followed on 22 October with allegations of a further drone strike killing eight civilians in Mopti and torture of detainees at Sevare, sharpening reprisal risk against anyone associated with the state or its partners; rating held at 4, all travel should be deferred.
BRIEF.SD: Sudan's war is in a drone-dominated phase: the UN Human Rights Office said on 23 October it had documented at least 306 deaths from drone strikes by both sides in the first three weeks of October alone, including a double-tap strike on a transport hub at Dibab in West Kordofan on 18 October that it now puts at 139 dead, army strikes on Nyala and RSF retaliation on Khartoum including the airport district on 19 October, and the 19 October strike on Abyei's Amiet market across the South Sudan border, which Khartoum denied on 22 October. The Geneva consultative meeting on 21 October produced no ceasefire track, the army retook the Bakori base in Blue Nile on 22 October while RSF and SPLM-N allies keep pressing the Kurmuk axis, and army-held Khartoum, Port Sudan and the eastern dams remain inside RSF drone range. Rating 4 retained with trend rising on the scale and reach of civilian-targeted strikes between 10 and 24 October; there is no basis for any corporate travel.
BRIEF.SS: South Sudan is absorbing direct spillover from Sudan's drone war: the 19 October strike on Amiet market and Todach in Abyei killed at least 80 by UNISFA's verified count on 22 October and 153 by the Abyei administration's figure given to Reuters, with many still missing; the UN Security Council condemned the attack in the strongest terms on 23 October, demanded an investigation and reaffirmed Abyei's demilitarised status, while Khartoum denied on 22 October that its armed forces were involved after Juba summoned Sudan's ambassador. Juba has no means to deter further strikes on RSF supply corridors through its territory, and internally the 9 October Rumbek fighting (71 dead by the government's preliminary count) showed how quickly intercommunal violence can engulf a state capital while Machar remains on trial and a 22 December election timetable few observers expect to hold approaches. Juba itself is calmer; expect further flashpoints in Abyei, Lakes, Jonglei and Upper Nile as the dry season opens roads to armed movement. Rating 4 retained, trend rising.
BRIEF.SO: As of 24 October, Laftagareen-aligned Darawish forces still hold Berdale, Dinsoor, Buurhakaba, Qansaxdheere and Awdiinle after their 15–17 October sweep through Bay region, leaving Baidoa as the only major town under the federally backed South West administration, which has announced a counteroffensive starting with Buurhakaba; the Mogadishu–Baidoa road remains cut and a fight for, or negotiated handover of, Baidoa is the base case. The electoral commission's 15 October timetable (parliament 15 April, president 15 May 2027) is rejected by the opposition, Puntland and Jubaland, sustaining the risk of armed political confrontation in Mogadishu, while in the north a UAE drone strike on 20 October in the Galgala pass and a US strike near Dhooble on 17 October precede an expected new Puntland offensive against al-Shabaab. IOM projects up to 874,000 flood displacements by December with the Shabelle above its high flood-risk level at Jowhar; no large or complex al-Shabaab attack in Mogadishu or at Aden Adde airport was wire-reported between 10 and 24 October, and rating 4, rising trend and no-go posture outside the airport/Halane enclave are retained.
BRIEF.ET: Tigray is easing but not settled: federal forces and the allied Tigray Peace Force hold Mekelle, Adigrat, Adwa and Axum, shops and banks were reopening in Mekelle on 22 October and schools are due to resume on 26 October under the six-month caretaker administration Abiy named on 16 October, yet the TPLF rejects it, Abiy warned Eritrea on 19 October of 'very severe consequences' if it keeps backing his enemies, and troops face each other along the Eritrean border. A new southern front has turned lethal: fighting between Oromia and Somali regional forces in Moyale that began on 21 October killed at least nine people by 23 October, spread to Gumi Eldallo, Wachile and Arero districts and pushed at least 2,500 people into Kenya, with gunfire still heard on 23 October. Rating 4 retained and trend flat: Tigray calmer, but the Moyale front, the Amhara Fano insurgency and the Eritrean confrontation all remain live, roads north of Addis remain unsafe and Addis Ababa functions under a heavy security posture.
BRIEF.ER: Eritrea remains a party to the Tigray confrontation in all but name: Ethiopia told the UN Security Council on 9 October that Eritrean forces had advanced up to 60 km into Tigray, Asmara asked the Council for Chapter VII measures on 10 October, Abiy warned on 19 October of 'very, very, very severe consequences' if Eritrea ignores his calls, and Asmara's 21 October foreign ministry statement restated a purely defensive posture, denied any invasion and accused Ethiopia's ruling party of coveting its coast. Rubio said on 17 October that troops are surging on both sides of the border and that this could turn into a broader conflict, while Eritrea's UN ambassador told US diplomats on 21 October there is no crisis; diplomatic ties remain severed. A cross-border escalation within weeks remains plausible and internal reporting from Eritrea is almost nil, so assume mobilisation, communications restrictions and no exit options if the border war widens. Rating 3 retained, trend flat between 10 and 24 October.
BRIEF.DJ: No violent security incident was recorded inside Djibouti between 10 and 24 October; the humanitarian load is the story, with UNHCR counting 3,836 refugees arrived from Yemen in Obock region by 17 October, an acute watery diarrhoea outbreak in the Markazi camp and the aftermath of the 8-9 October migrant shipwreck off Obock (139 dead, 84 missing per IOM), which now falls outside the two-week window. The exposure is external: Houthi forces fighting for Yemen's Red Sea coast keep the Bab el-Mandeb, Camp Lemonnier and the port within missile and drone range, and Djibouti and China jointly flagged a deteriorating Red Sea security situation on 22 October; the Ethiopia-Djibouti corridor runs through Afar, where fighting has decreased but not ended. Djibouti City and the ports operate normally; rating 2 retained, monitor corridor security in Afar, war-risk premiums and any Houthi targeting of shipping or foreign bases.
BRIEF.KE: Nairobi and the main business corridors are operating, but 23 October brought two shocks to the capital: an 18-storey building under construction collapsed onto occupied ground-floor shops in Eastleigh at about 13:40, with seven people reported missing, two injured and police firing tear gas at looters, and the health ministry announced a second Ebola death, a 65-year-old relative of the index patient who fell ill in quarantine, in a nine-case cluster that still shows no transmission outside the family and healthcare-worker group. In the north, fighting between Ethiopia's Oromia and Somali regional forces in Moyale has killed at least nine on the Ethiopian side, pushed at least 2,500 people into Kenya's Marsabit county and sent stray rounds into the Kenyan town, while a Special Operations Group raid near the Somali border reported on 21 October killed 11 al-Shabaab fighters said to be preparing an attack in Mandera. The US Level 3 advisory of 19 October keeps Garissa, Wajir, Mandera, Lamu and Tana River at Do Not Travel, the 14 October fuel price rise adds a cost-of-living trigger and the 2027 election cycle is under way; rating 3 retained, trend flat.
BRIEF.CD: Rating held at 4. Twelve days after Joseph Kabila launched the Front pour la Refondation de la Nation (FRN) in Goma, absorbing AFC/M23 and pledging to end 'tyranny' by force (Reuters, 12 Oct), the political-military confrontation has hardened: Kinshasa has banned 13 parties including Kabila's PPRD (DW, 17 Oct), the African Union warned on 20 October against any seizure of power by force, and Belgium's foreign minister condemned the FRN as 'unacceptable' on 21 October, while fighting between FRN/M23 and FARDC-Wazalendo continues with drones and artillery in the South Kivu highlands (Walungu/Kaziba) and foothills toward Uvira and in Masisi, and no Kagame-Tshisekedi signing or ceasefire breakthrough has materialised. The Bundibugyo Ebola outbreak stood at 9,765 confirmed cases and 4,727 deaths across eight provinces on 23 October (UN News), with Nigeria confirming its first case on 20 October and Kenya nine, and WHO warning of resurgence if the response slackens; separately about 300 Chinese nationals were detained in Kolwezi between 12 and 16 October in an illegal-mining crackdown (Bloomberg), a reminder that enforcement actions in the copper belt can affect foreign staff. Goma, Bukavu, Uvira and all of North/South Kivu and Ituri remain no-go; Kinshasa and Lubumbashi/Kolwezi are operable with advance planning but carry elevated risk of politically driven unrest, arbitrary detention of persons linked to banned parties, document checks on expatriate mine workers and sudden movement restrictions between 10 and 24 October.
BRIEF.BR: Brazil votes on Sunday 25 October in a presidential runoff that is a statistical dead heat: Datafolha published a 50-50 tie on 22 October and the final TV Globo debate on 23 October left the share of undecided voters doubling to 14% (AFP, 23 Oct), while each camp has a petition pending at the Superior Electoral Court to disqualify the other, so a narrow result is likely to be contested in court and on the street. Federal troops will patrol 15 Rio de Janeiro municipalities on polling day alongside more than 20,000 state police (Agência Brasil, 23 Oct), reflecting the electoral court's concern about gang- and militia-controlled areas. Rating held at 2 between 10 and 24 October: the only wire-confirmed lethal incident in the window was the 19 October Military Police shooting of a Queimados municipal secretary on Avenida Brasil, with no attacks on foreigners or business districts; trend rising for the runoff weekend and any disputed count.
BRIEF.CO: President de la Espriella's offensive against the ELN and FARC dissidents is escalating on both sides: a 22 October air strike on an ELN camp in El Tambo, Cauca killed nine guerrillas including regional commander alias Marcos Pacífico (DW, 23 Oct), the fifth bombing of his term, while guerrillas hit back at fixed police positions, wounding six officers in a drone-bomb attack on the Pelaya station in Cesar on 21 October (AP, 21 Oct) after the 12 October car bomb at the El Bordo toll plaza on the Pan-American Highway (AP, 12 Oct). The president replaced his interior minister on 21-22 October after the budget bill collapsed in Congress, adding political turbulence to the security push. Bogotá, Medellín and Cartagena recorded no wire-confirmed attack between 10 and 24 October; rating held at 3 with the trend rising because retaliation against security forces and infrastructure in the south-west, Catatumbo and the Cesar-Arauca corridor is the established pattern after each strike.
BRIEF.VE: The first nationwide opposition protest in nearly two years on 22 October passed without wire-reported violence, with thousands marching in Caracas, Valencia, Maracay, San Cristóbal and Maracaibo for a 2027 election date and the release of political prisoners while the ruling party staged a rival march from the same square (Reuters, 22 Oct); Machado's party afterwards said seven marchers were detained by the Bolivarian National Police (AFP, 23 Oct). The US-backed talks closed their third round on 21 October with an agreement to review laws that bar opposition figures from office, and on 22 October acting President Delcy Rodríguez received opposition delegation head Dinorah Figuera for the first time (DW, 23 Oct), but no election date has been set. No US military action, deadly unrest or detention of a foreign national was wire-confirmed between 10 and 24 October; rating held at 3 because the transition remains unscheduled and the street is now an active lever for both sides.
